(No specific source files were provided for this section.) In the absence of specific code, this section refers to common UI patterns implemented across the Rocket.Chat application to enhance user experience during data loading or processing. These patterns typically involve displaying "skeleton" screens, which are simplified wireframe versions of the content that will eventually load, or using various loading indicators like spinners. These visual cues inform the user that content is on its way, preventing perceived delays and improving the responsiveness of the interface. Such implementations are usually handled by dedicated UI components or integrated within data-fetching logic to conditionally render loading states.

Sidebar, Navigation & Client-Side Router.text: The Rocket.Chat client-side navigation primarily revolves around the main sidebar and a dynamic side panel. The sidebar displays various items, such as channels, direct messages, and discussions, each represented by a `SidebarV2Item` from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`. These items can take different visual forms, or 'variants', to convey information like unread status, timestamps, and avatars. The system also includes a 'Side Panel' which serves as a sub-navigation or detailed view, often used for displaying children of a main room or filtered lists. While the provided files detail the structure and rendering of sidebar and side panel items, the overarching client-side routing mechanism that handles `href` navigation is not explicitly defined within these files.

The Rocket.Chat sidebar supports several item variants to accommodate different display needs and information density. These variants are built upon the `SidebarV2Item` component from `@rocket.chat/fuselage` and manage their menu visibility using a local `useState` hook, triggered by `onFocus` or `onPointerEnter` events. A common `IconButton` with a 'kebab' icon is used to reveal the menu.

*   **`Extended`**: Defined in `apps/meteor/client/sidebar/Item/Extended.tsx`, this variant provides the most detailed view. It utilizes `SidebarV2ItemCol`, `SidebarV2ItemRow`, `SidebarV2ItemTitle`, `SidebarV2ItemTimestamp`, and `SidebarV2ItemContent` to display an avatar, title, timestamp (formatted by `useShortTimeAgo` from `apps/meteor/client/hooks/useTimeAgo.ts`), subtitle, badges, and actions.
*   **`Medium`**: Found in `apps/meteor/client/sidebar/Item/Medium.tsx`, this variant offers a balanced view, including an avatar, title, badges, and actions, but without the detailed subtitle and timestamp of the `Extended` variant.
*   **`Condensed`**: Implemented in `apps/meteor/client/sidebar/Item/Condensed.tsx`, this is the most compact variant, primarily showing an avatar, title, badges, and actions, suitable for high-density lists.
*   **`SidebarItem`**: Located in `apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidebar/RoomList/SidebarItem.tsx`, this component is specifically designed for displaying `SubscriptionWithRoom` objects in the room list. It integrates `RoomAvatar` from `@rocket.chat/ui-avatar` for room-specific avatars and shares a similar structure to the `Condensed` and `Medium` variants, including title, badges, actions, and menu functionality.

Several hooks are crucial for dynamically rendering and managing sidebar items:

*   **`useUnreadDisplay`**: This hook, found in both `apps/meteor/client/sidebar/hooks/useUnreadDisplay.ts` and `apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidebar/hooks/useUnreadDisplay.ts`, processes `UnreadData` to determine the unread count, title, and variant for badges. It leverages `getSubscriptionUnreadData` from `lib/getSubscriptionUnreadData.ts` and `useTranslation` to provide localized unread information. This hook is notably used by `SidebarItemBadges` in `apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidebar/badges/SidebarItemBadges.tsx` to render `UnreadBadge` and `InvitationBadge` components.
*   **`useAvatarTemplate`**: Defined in `apps/meteor/client/sidebar/hooks/useAvatarTemplate.tsx`, this hook dynamically determines the appropriate `RoomAvatar` component and its size ('x36', 'x28', or 'x20') based on user preferences for `sidebarViewMode` and `sidebarDisplayAvatar`. It returns a memoized `ComponentType` that renders a `RoomAvatar` for a given `SubscriptionWithRoom`.
*   **`useChannelsChildrenList`**: Located in `apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidepanel/hooks/useChannelsChildrenList.ts`, this hook fetches and sorts `SubscriptionWithRoom` records from the `Subscriptions` store. It's used to populate lists of channels, discussions, or team rooms that are children of a specific parent room (`parentRid`) or belong to a `teamId`. The hook ensures that the main room (e.g., main team room or parent's discussion room) is always at the top of the list, followed by other rooms sorted by `lm` (last message timestamp), with an option to prioritize unread rooms.

The Side Panel provides a secondary navigation or detailed view, often used to display related rooms or filtered lists. Its core logic is encapsulated in `SidePanelInternal` (`apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidepanel/SidePanelInternal.tsx`).

The `SidePanelInternal` component renders a `Sidepanel` from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`, featuring a `SidepanelHeader` with a title, a back button (on tablets via `useLayout`), and an 'Unread' toggle switch. It efficiently displays lists of rooms using `VirtualizedScrollbars` and `Virtuoso` for virtualization, which renders `SidepanelListItem` components. The actual content for each item is provided by an `ItemContentComponent` prop, which receives `room`, `openedRoom` (from `useOpenedRoom`), and `isRoomFilter` props.

The `SidePanel` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidepanel/SidePanel.tsx`) is a memoized instance created by `createSidePanel` from `SidePanelInternal.tsx`, specifically configured with `RoomSidePanelItem` (not provided in source, but inferred as the item content component for rooms).

Individual items within the Side Panel are often rendered using `SidePanelItem` (`apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidepanel/SidepanelItem/SidepanelItem.tsx`). This component is similar to the `Extended` sidebar item, displaying an avatar, title, timestamp (using `useShortTimeAgo`), subtitle, badges, and a menu. It also handles `onClick` events to toggle the main sidebar when a new item is selected, leveraging `useLayout`.

The provided source files do not contain specific implementations or details regarding the Navbar component or the process of channel creation. These functionalities are likely handled by other parts of the Rocket.Chat codebase not included in this context.

While sidebar and side panel items include an `href` prop, indicating their role in navigation, the underlying client-side routing mechanism (e.g., how `href` values are translated into view changes or how routes are managed) is not detailed in the provided source files. The components focus on rendering the navigable elements rather than the routing logic itself.

The provided source files do not contain information about the implementation of banners or how the sidebar is organized into distinct sections beyond the individual item variants. The files primarily focus on the structure and behavior of individual sidebar and side panel list items.

Administration Panel.text: The Administration Panel in Rocket.Chat provides a centralized interface for managing various aspects of the workspace. It is rendered by the `AdministrationLayout` component located at `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/AdministrationLayout.tsx`. This layout acts as a container, embedding the `AdminSidebar` for navigation and rendering the specific administration content as its children.

The layout of the administration panel is defined by `AdministrationLayout` (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/AdministrationLayout.tsx`). It utilizes a `SidebarPortal` to inject the `AdminSidebar` component, ensuring consistent navigation. The `AdminSidebar` dynamically generates its menu items using the `createSidebarItems` utility, which is exposed as `registerAdminSidebarItem`, `unregisterSidebarItem`, `getAdminSidebarItems`, and `subscribeToAdminSidebarItems` in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`. Each sidebar item, such as "Workspace", "Subscription", "Users", or "Settings", includes a `permissionGranted` function. This function leverages client-side authorization helpers like `hasPermission`, `hasAtLeastOnePermission`, and `hasAllPermission` from `app/authorization/client` to determine if the currently logged-in user has the necessary permissions to view and access that specific section. For instance, the "Users" section requires the `view-user-administration` permission.

The settings editor is a core part of the administration panel, allowing administrators to configure various aspects of Rocket.Chat. Individual settings are rendered by the `MemoizedSetting` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/settings/Setting/MemoizedSetting.tsx`). This component is responsible for displaying the setting's label, hint, and the appropriate input field based on its `type` property (e.g., `boolean`, `string`, `int`, `select`, `color`, `asset`, `action`). It dynamically selects an input component from `inputsByType`, which maps setting types to specific React components like `BooleanSettingInput`, `StringSettingInput`, `ColorSettingInput`, etc., found within the `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/settings/Setting/inputs/` directory. On the backend, settings are managed by the `SettingsRaw` model (`packages/models/src/models/Settings.ts`), which extends `BaseRaw` for MongoDB interactions. This model provides methods like `getValueById`, `updateValueById`, `resetValueById`, and `updateValueAndEditorById` to interact with the `settings` collection in the database. Server-side, a cache is maintained for setting values using `setValue` and `getValue` in `apps/meteor/app/settings/server/raw.ts` to optimize access. Furthermore, the `useHasSettingModule` hook (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/settings/hooks/useHasSettingModule.ts`) determines if a specific setting is available based on the active license modules. It uses `useLicenseBase` from `@rocket.chat/ui-client` to check if the workspace is an enterprise instance and if all required `modules` for a given setting are active.

The Subscription section, accessible via `/admin/subscription`, provides details about the workspace's Rocket.Chat license. Its visibility is controlled by the `hasPermission('manage-cloud')` check in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`. The `PlanTag` component (`apps/meteor/client/components/PlanTag.tsx`) displays the current plan (e.g., "Community", "Development", or other license tags) by consuming license data from the `useLicense` hook provided by `@rocket.chat/ui-client`. Similarly, the `VersionTag` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/workspace/VersionCard/components/VersionTag.tsx`) indicates the status of the Rocket.Chat version (e.g., "Outdated", "Latest", "New_version_available") using `Tag` components from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`. Utility links related to subscription management, such as `CONTACT_SALES_LINK`, `PRICING_LINK`, `DOWNGRADE_LINK`, `TRIAL_LINK`, and `GET_ADDONS_LINK`, are defined in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/subscription/utils/links.ts`, leveraging the global `links` object.

The Integrations section allows administrators to configure various incoming and outgoing integrations. Access to this section is granted if the user has at least one of several permissions, including `manage-outgoing-integrations`, `manage-own-outgoing-integrations`, `manage-incoming-integrations`, or `manage-own-incoming-integrations`, as defined in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`. For developers working with incoming integrations, the `useExampleData` hook (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/integrations/hooks/useExampleIncomingData.tsx`) provides example JSON payloads and `curl` commands. This hook generates sample data, including text and attachments, and constructs a `curl` command for testing, utilizing `useAbsoluteUrl` to resolve image URLs.

The Permissions section, found at `/admin/permissions`, enables fine-grained control over user access and capabilities. Its visibility is determined by the `hasAtLeastOnePermission(['access-permissions', 'access-setting-permissions'])` check in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`. The core mechanism for checking user permissions throughout the application, including for sidebar item visibility, is provided by `hasPermission`, `hasAtLeastOnePermission`, and `hasAllPermission` from `app/authorization/client`. On the client-side, the `usePermission` hook (`packages/ui-contexts/src/hooks/usePermission.ts`) allows React components to subscribe to and reactively query specific permissions for a given scope, leveraging the `AuthorizationContext` and `useSyncExternalStore` for efficient updates.

User management functionalities are accessible through dedicated sections in the administration panel. The "Users" section (`/admin/users`) requires the `view-user-administration` permission, while the "Invites" section (`/admin/invites`) requires `create-invite-links`. Additionally, "User_Status" (`/admin/user-status`) requires `manage-user-status` permission. These permissions are checked via `hasPermission` or `hasAtLeastOnePermission` as defined in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`, ensuring that only authorized administrators can access these features.

The Moderation console, located at `/admin/moderation`, provides tools for content moderation. This section is tagged as "Beta" in the sidebar and is only visible to users who possess the `view-moderation-console` permission, as specified in `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/sidebarItems.ts`.

The administration panel extensively uses shared UI primitives to maintain a consistent look and feel. Components from `@rocket.chat/fuselage` like `Box`, `Callout`, `Field`, `Margins`, `Tag` are frequently used, as seen in `MemoizedSetting.tsx`, `PlanTag.tsx`, and `VersionTag.tsx`. For settings, a variety of specialized input components are used, such as `BooleanSettingInput`, `StringSettingInput`, `ColorSettingInput`, `SelectSettingInput`, and `AssetSettingInput`, all located under `apps/meteor/client/views/admin/settings/Setting/inputs/`. These inputs adhere to a common `SettingInputProps` interface (`apps/meteor/client/views/admin/settings/Setting/inputs/types.ts`), ensuring consistency in how setting values are handled and updated.

Omnichannel Live Chat UI.text: The Omnichannel Live Chat UI in Rocket.Chat provides a comprehensive interface for managing live chat operations. It is structured around a sidebar navigation system, defined in `apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/sidebarItems.tsx`, which registers various modules such as 'Contact_Center', 'Analytics', 'Real_Time_Monitoring', 'Managers', 'Agents', 'Departments', 'Custom_Fields', 'Livechat_Triggers', 'Livechat_Installation', 'Livechat_Appearance', 'Webhooks', 'Business_Hours', and 'Security_and_privacy'. Each sidebar item's visibility is controlled by specific permissions, ensuring users only access relevant sections, for example, `hasPermission('view-omnichannel-contact-center')` for the Contact Center. This modular approach allows for a tailored user experience based on roles and responsibilities.

Navigation within the Omnichannel UI is managed through a combination of hooks and the core router. The `useOmnichannelDirectoryRouter` hook, found in `apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/directory/hooks/useOmnichannelDirectoryRouter.ts`, provides a specialized `navigate` function that ensures routing stays within valid Omnichannel directory routes, specifically `omnichannel-directory` or `omnichannel-current-chats`. Similarly, the `useContactRoute` hook in `apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/hooks/useContactRoute.ts` handles navigation related to contact information. It automatically sets route parameters like `tab: 'contacts'` and `context: 'details'` when navigating to contact-related views within the directory or current chats, ensuring a consistent context for contact interactions. The `sidebarItems.tsx` file directly links navigation paths (e.g., `/omnichannel/current`) to specific UI sections, leveraging the `useRouter` from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts`.

Managing contact information is a central aspect of the Omnichannel UI. The `EditContactInfo` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/contactInfo/EditContactInfo.tsx`) facilitates the creation and modification of live chat contacts. This component uses `react-hook-form` for managing form state, including fields for `name`, `emails`, `phones`, `customFields`, and `contactManager`. It dynamically handles multiple email and phone entries using `useFieldArray`. Validation includes format checks via `@rocket.chat/tools`'s `validateEmail` and existence checks against the `/v1/omnichannel/contacts.checkExistence` endpoint to prevent duplicate emails or phone numbers. Custom fields are integrated using `CustomFieldsForm` and metadata fetched via `useCustomFieldsMetadata`. In cases where a contact cannot be found, the `ContactInfoError` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/contactInfo/ContactInfoError.tsx`) provides a user-friendly error display within a `ContextualbarDialog`.

Autocomplete components enhance user experience by simplifying data entry. The `AutoCompleteDepartment` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/components/AutoCompleteDepartment.tsx`) is a prime example, providing a paginated and filtered selection for departments. It leverages `@rocket.chat/fuselage`'s `PaginatedSelectFiltered` and `useDebouncedValue` for efficient filtering. Department data is fetched using the `useDepartmentsList` hook, which supports various filtering options such as `onlyMyDepartments`, `haveAll`, `haveNone`, `excludeId`, `showArchived`, and `unitId`. This allows agents and managers to quickly select relevant departments based on their context and permissions.

Priorities are used to categorize and manage live chat conversations. The `useOmnichannelPriorities` hook (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/hooks/useOmnichannelPriorities.ts`) provides access to the configured live chat priorities, typically sourced from a broader Omnichannel context. Visual representation of these priorities is handled by the `PriorityIcon` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/priorities/PriorityIcon.tsx`). This component takes a `LivechatPriorityWeight` level and, using the `useOmnichannelPrioritiesConfig` hook, determines the appropriate icon name, color, and display name to render, allowing for clear visual identification of chat priority levels throughout the UI.

The Omnichannel UI provides robust tools for automating responses and integrating with external services through triggers and webhooks.

**Triggers:** The `EditTrigger` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/triggers/EditTrigger.tsx`) allows administrators to create and modify live chat triggers. Triggers are defined by `conditions` (e.g., `page-url`) and `actions` (e.g., `send-message`, `use-external-service`). The component uses `react-hook-form` and `useFieldArray` to manage these dynamic lists of conditions and actions. Actions are normalized by the `getDefaultAction` function to ensure consistent parameter structures. Triggers are saved via a `POST` request to the `/v1/livechat/triggers` endpoint, and the UI ensures relevant queries are invalidated to reflect changes.

**Webhooks:** The `WebhooksPage` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/webhooks/WebhooksPage.tsx`) configures live chat webhooks. It allows setting a `Livechat_webhookUrl`, `Livechat_secret_token`, and `Livechat_http_timeout`. Users can select specific events to trigger webhooks, such as `Livechat_webhook_on_start`, `Livechat_webhook_on_close`, or `Livechat_webhook_on_visitor_message`. Configurations are saved by sending a `POST` request to the `/v1/omnichannel/integrations` endpoint. The page also includes functionality to test the webhook configuration via the `/v1/livechat/webhook.test` endpoint.

Real-time monitoring capabilities are crucial for overseeing live chat operations. The `MonitorsTable` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/omnichannel/monitors/MonitorsTable.tsx`) provides an interface for managing live chat monitors. It displays a paginated and sortable list of monitors using `GenericTable`, `usePagination`, and `useSort`. Users can add new monitors by selecting a username via `UserAutoComplete` and submitting a `POST` request to `/v1/livechat/monitors.create`. Existing monitors can be removed with a `POST` request to `/v1/livechat/monitors.delete`, preceded by a confirmation modal. Data for the table is fetched from the `/v1/livechat/monitors` endpoint, and `useQueryClient` ensures the UI is updated after add/remove operations. The 'Real_Time_Monitoring' section in the sidebar, defined in `sidebarItems.tsx`, grants access to this functionality based on the `view-livechat-real-time-monitoring` permission.

Based on the provided source files, there is no direct information or components related to an 'Outbound Messaging Wizard'. This functionality might be implemented in other parts of the codebase or not yet present in the provided context.

UI Kit Blocks, Fuselage Renderer & Playg.section: UI Kit Blocks, Fuselage Renderer & Playground
UI Kit Blocks, Fuselage Renderer & Playg.text: The Rocket.Chat UI Kit provides a robust system for defining and rendering UI components across different surfaces. It separates the abstract definition of UI elements (blocks) from their concrete rendering implementation. The `pkg:ui-kit` package defines the block types, while `pkg:fuselage-ui-kit` provides the Fuselage-specific rendering logic. This architecture allows for consistent UI definitions that can be rendered natively in various environments, including the web client, mobile apps, and even within the server for certain contexts. The 'Playground' (though not explicitly detailed in provided files) serves as an application to demonstrate and test these UI Kit blocks and their Fuselage rendering.

The `pkg:ui-kit` package establishes the foundational types for UI components. At its core, `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/TextObject.ts` defines `TextObject` as a union of `PlainText` and `Markdown` types. `PlainText` (from `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/text/PlainText.ts`) represents simple text, optionally with emoji support and internationalization capabilities via `WithTranslations`. `TextObjectType` (from `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/TextObjectType.ts`) provides constants like `PLAIN_TEXT` and `MRKDWN` for identifying these text types. Interactive elements are defined by `BlockElement` (from `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/BlockElement.ts`), which is a comprehensive union type encompassing various input controls (e.g., `ButtonElement`, `PlainTextInputElement`, `StaticSelectElement`, `DatePickerElement`, `ToggleSwitchElement`, etc.). Blocks that can trigger actions or have associated state are augmented by the `Actionable` type (from `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/Actionable.ts`), which adds properties like `appId`, `blockId`, `actionId`, `confirm` dialogs, and `dispatchActionConfig`. All layout blocks share common properties defined by `LayoutBlockish` (from `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/LayoutBlockish.ts`), such as optional `appId` and `blockId`. The `BlockContext` enum (from `packages/ui-kit/src/rendering/BlockContext.ts`) defines various contexts (e.g., `NONE`, `BLOCK`, `SECTION`, `ACTION`, `FORM`, `CONTEXT`) that influence how blocks and elements are rendered and behave, particularly regarding state management and action dispatching.

The `pkg:fuselage-ui-kit` package provides the concrete implementations for rendering UI Kit blocks into Fuselage React components. The abstract `SurfaceRenderer` class (from `packages/ui-kit/src/rendering/SurfaceRenderer.ts`) is the cornerstone, defining the interface for rendering various block types and elements. Concrete renderers like `BannerSurfaceRenderer`, `FuselageMessageSurfaceRenderer`, `ModalSurfaceRenderer`, and `ContextualBarSurfaceRenderer` (all exported from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/surfaces/index.ts`) extend `SurfaceRenderer` to handle specific UI surfaces. Each renderer is initialized with a set of `allowedLayoutBlockTypes` to ensure only relevant blocks are processed for a given surface. The `render` method of `SurfaceRenderer` takes an array of `Block` objects, resolves conditional blocks using `resolveConditionalBlocks`, filters them by `isAllowedLayoutBlock`, and then maps them using `renderLayoutBlock(this)`. It also provides specialized methods like `renderTextObject`, `renderActionsBlockElement`, `renderContextBlockElement`, `renderInputBlockElement`, and `renderSectionAccessoryBlockElement`, which delegate to `renderBlockElement` or `renderTextObject` with the appropriate `BlockContext`. For text objects, `SurfaceRenderer` requires abstract implementations for `plain_text` and `mrkdwn` methods, which concrete renderers must provide to convert `PlainText` and `Markdown` objects into Fuselage-compatible output. The `createSurfaceRenderer` utility (from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/surfaces/createSurfaceRenderer.ts`, exported via `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/surfaces/index.ts`) wraps a Fuselage component (e.g., `BannerSurface`, `MessageSurface`) with a specific `SurfaceRenderer` instance to create ready-to-use React components like `UiKitBanner`, `UiKitMessage`, `UiKitModal`, and `UiKitContextualBar`. Additionally, the `useStringFromTextObject` hook (from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/hooks/useStringFromTextObject.ts`) assists in translating `TextObject` instances into displayable strings, leveraging `useAppTranslation` for internationalization.

Action management for UI Kit elements is primarily handled by the `useUiKitState` hook (from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/hooks/useUiKitState.ts`). This hook is designed to manage the state (`value`, `loading`, `error`) of `ActionableElement`s within UI Kit blocks. It consumes the `UiKitContext` to access global UI Kit state, including `values` (current form values), `errors`, `action` (the dispatch function for actions), `updateState` (for updating local state), `appId`, and `viewId`. When an interactive element's value changes, `useUiKitState` determines the appropriate action function to call: `actionFunction` for general actions, `noLoadStateActionFunction` for text inputs with `on_character_entered` dispatch config (to avoid losing focus), or `stateFunction` for simple state updates. These functions update the internal state via `setValue` and then call `updateState` and/or `action` from the `UiKitContext`, passing relevant `blockId`, `actionId`, `appId`, `value`, `viewId`, and `dispatchActionConfig`. The behavior of the action function is also influenced by the `BlockContext` (e.g., `BlockContext.SECTION` or `BlockContext.ACTION` trigger `actionFunction`). The `InputBlock` component (from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/blocks/InputBlock.tsx`) demonstrates this integration, using `useUiKitState` to manage the state of its `inputElement` and display `FieldError` messages based on the `error` returned by the hook. It also uses the `surfaceRenderer` to render the `block.label` and `block.hint` `TextObject`s.

While specific files for a 'UIKit Playground Application' are not provided, its role within the ecosystem is to serve as a development and demonstration environment. It would leverage the `UiKit*` React components (e.g., `UiKitBanner`, `UiKitMessage`, `UiKitModal`, `UiKitContextualBar`) exported from `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/src/surfaces/index.ts`. Developers would use the playground to render various UI Kit block structures, interact with them, and observe their behavior, including state changes managed by `useUiKitState` and action dispatches. This application would be crucial for testing new UI Kit blocks, verifying rendering consistency across different surfaces, and showcasing the capabilities of the UI Kit system without needing to integrate them into a full Rocket.Chat client application.

Avatars, Theming, Assets & Favicon.text: The Rocket.Chat codebase manages user and room representation through a structured avatar component hierarchy, ensures visual consistency with theming principles (though not explicitly detailed in these files, it's an underlying concept for UI components), and handles various assets, most notably the dynamic favicon system. This document details the implementation of these core UI elements, from the foundational `BaseAvatar` component to the intricate favicon badging mechanism and server-side asset configurations.

The avatar system is built around a clear component hierarchy, promoting reusability and separation of concerns. The foundational component is `BaseAvatar` located at `packages/ui-avatar/src/components/BaseAvatar.tsx`. This component is responsible for rendering an image from a given `url`, handling `onLoad` and `onError` events, and displaying a `@rocket.chat/fuselage` `Skeleton` if the image fails to load or is still loading. It directly utilizes the `Avatar` and `Skeleton` components from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`.

Building upon `BaseAvatar`, specialized avatar components cater to different entities:

*   `UserAvatar` (`packages/ui-avatar/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx`): Renders avatars for users. It accepts either a `username` or `userId` and optionally an `etag`. It uses the `useUserAvatarPath` hook from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts` to resolve the avatar URL if not explicitly provided, then passes it to `BaseAvatar`.
*   `RoomAvatar` (`packages/ui-avatar/src/components/RoomAvatar.tsx`): Renders avatars for rooms. It takes a `room` object and resolves its avatar URL using the `useRoomAvatarPath` hook from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts`, before rendering with `BaseAvatar`.
*   `AppAvatar` (`packages/ui-avatar/src/components/AppAvatar.tsx`): Designed for application icons. It accepts `iconFileContent` or `iconFileData` (base64 encoded) to construct the image URL, which is then passed to `BaseAvatar`.
*   `MessageAvatar` (`packages/ui-avatar/src/components/MessageAvatar.tsx`): A higher-level component used within messages. It can render either an `emoji` (wrapped in an `AvatarContainer` from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`) or a `UserAvatar` based on the provided `avatarUrl` and `username`.

The favicon badge system allows for dynamic updates to the browser's favicon, typically to display unread counts or status indicators. The core logic resides in `packages/favicon/src/index.ts` and `packages/favicon/src/badge.ts`.

The `manageFavicon` function in `packages/favicon/src/index.ts` is the entry point for this system. Upon initialization, it identifies all `<link rel="icon">` elements in the document head via `getFavicons`. It then fetches the current favicon image using `fetchFaviconImage` and sets up an `HTMLCanvasElement` for rendering. The `updateOrCollect` function, returned by `manageFavicon`, is responsible for triggering the favicon update process.

When `updateOrCollect` is called with a `Badge` value (a number or string), it invokes `renderAndUpdate`. This function clears the canvas, draws the base favicon image, and then delegates the badge drawing to `drawBadge` from `packages/favicon/src/badge.ts`. The `drawBadge` function calculates the badge text (`getBadgeText`) and style (`getBadgeStyle`) based on the badge value, then draws a dynamically sized and colored badge (circle or rounded rectangle) onto the canvas context. Finally, `renderAndUpdate` converts the canvas content to a data URL and updates the `href` attribute of all identified favicon `<link>` elements, effectively changing the browser's favicon.

Server-side asset settings provide administrative control over certain asset-related features. The `createAssetsSettings` function in `apps/meteor/server/settings/assets.ts` registers a setting group named 'Assets'. Within this group, the `Assets_SvgFavicon_Enable` boolean setting is defined, allowing administrators to enable or disable SVG favicons. This setting is managed through the `settingsRegistry` and provides a server-side configuration point for asset behavior, though its direct interaction with the client-side favicon rendering (as described in `packages/favicon`) is not explicitly shown in the provided client-side code.

The avatar and favicon implementations demonstrate several key design principles:

*   **Modularity and Reusability**: The `BaseAvatar` component serves as a highly reusable foundation, abstracting common avatar rendering logic. Specialized components like `UserAvatar`, `RoomAvatar`, and `AppAvatar` then build upon this base, focusing on entity-specific data retrieval.
*   **Separation of Concerns**: The `packages/ui-avatar` module is solely responsible for rendering avatars, while `packages/favicon` handles the distinct logic of favicon management and badging. Server-side settings for assets are kept separate in `apps/meteor/server/settings/assets.ts`.
*   **Context-Driven Data**: Avatar URLs for users and rooms are fetched using hooks (`useUserAvatarPath`, `useRoomAvatarPath`) from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts`. This pattern decouples the UI components from the specific data fetching mechanisms, making them more flexible and testable.
*   **Progressive Enhancement/Robustness**: `BaseAvatar` gracefully handles image loading failures or pending states by rendering a `Skeleton`, ensuring a consistent user experience even when assets are unavailable or slow to load. The favicon system also includes error handling for image loading and canvas context creation.

VoIP, Media Calls & Call History.text: The Rocket.Chat codebase handles Voice over IP (VoIP) and media calls, including features like audio, screen sharing, call transfer, and hold. This functionality is structured across several packages, separating the user interface context, the core media signaling logic, and enterprise-specific server-side services. The system manages the lifecycle of a call, from initiation and ringing to active communication and termination, while also providing mechanisms for call history and user interaction within the UI.

The `ui-voip` package provides the React contexts necessary for managing the UI state and interactions related to media calls. The `MediaCallViewContext` (`packages/ui-voip/src/context/MediaCallViewContext.ts`) exposes the `sessionState` (e.g., `closed`, `ringing`, `ongoing`, `calling` as seen in `packages/ui-voip/src/providers/MockedMediaCallProvider.tsx`) and a set of UI actions such as `onMute`, `onHold`, `onEndCall`, `onCall`, `onAccept`, and `onToggleScreenSharing`. It also provides access to `MediaCallStreams` for local and remote screen sharing. The `MediaCallInstanceContext` (`packages/ui-voip/src/context/MediaCallInstanceContext.ts`) is responsible for providing the underlying `MediaSignalingSession` instance and a `signalEmitter` for internal UI events (e.g., `toggleWidget`). It also includes utilities like `getAutocompleteOptions` for peer selection. These contexts work together to abstract the complex signaling logic from the presentation layer, allowing the UI to react to call state changes and trigger call actions.

The core logic for establishing and managing media calls resides in the `@rocket.chat/media-signaling` package. The `MediaSignalingSession` is the central component, responsible for orchestrating the call lifecycle. It utilizes a `MediaSignalTransport` to send `ClientMediaSignal` messages and process incoming `ServerMediaSignal` messages. The `useMediaSessionInstance` hook (`packages/ui-voip/src/providers/useMediaSessionInstance.ts`) in `ui-voip` is crucial for integrating this into the React application. This hook initializes and manages a `MediaSignalingSession` instance via a `MediaSessionStore`. It configures the session with a `MediaCallWebRTCProcessor` (which uses `useIceServers` and `VoIP_TeamCollab_Ice_Gathering_Timeout` from settings) for WebRTC handling. Client signals are sent using `writeStream('notify-user', ...)` and server signals are received by subscribing to `notifyUserStream(`${userId}/media-signal`, ...)` (`packages/ui-voip/src/providers/useMediaSessionInstance.ts`). The `ClientMediaCall` class (`packages/media-signaling/src/lib/Call.ts`) within the signaling package defines the detailed state (`CallState`), role (`CallRole`), contact, and features (`CallFeature` like 'audio', 'screen-share', 'transfer', 'hold') of an individual call, managing its negotiation via a `NegotiationManager` and interacting with the `IWebRTCProcessor`. It also tracks `ClientState` and `ClientContractState` (`packages/media-signaling/src/definition/client.ts`) to represent the client's involvement and agreement status in a call. Logging is handled by `IMediaSignalLogger` (`packages/media-signaling/src/definition/logger.ts`).

The `ee/media-calls` package provides server-side components and definitions specifically for enterprise media call features. It defines interfaces like `IMediaCallCastDirector` and `IMediaCallServer` (`ee/packages/media-calls/src/server/injection.ts`), which are responsible for managing call routing, server-side call state, and interactions with external systems (e.g., SIP gateways). The `getCastDirector` and `getMediaCallServer` functions provide access to these injected instances. The `InternalCallParams` type (`ee/packages/media-calls/src/definition/common.ts`) outlines the necessary parameters for initiating calls internally, including caller, callee, requested service, and supported features. `CallRejectedError` is a specific error type for handling call rejections. The package also defines standard `CallFeature` sets, such as `DEFAULT_CALL_FEATURES` (['audio']) and `SIP_CALL_FEATURES` (['audio', 'transfer', 'hold']) (`ee/packages/media-calls/src/constants.ts`), indicating the capabilities supported by different call types. A dedicated `Logger` (`ee/packages/media-calls/src/logger.ts`) is used for server-side media call events.

The provided source files do not contain specific details or implementations for a 'Call History Contextual Bar'. This functionality would typically involve storing call metadata (e.g., caller, callee, duration, outcome) in a database and exposing it through a UI component, likely leveraging existing Rocket.Chat UI patterns for contextual information within a room or user profile.

Video Conferencing Service & UI.text: The video conferencing service in Rocket.Chat provides both the user interface components and the underlying data model for managing calls. It encompasses shared UI elements for displaying call information and popups, dedicated routing for conference pages, and a robust model layer to persist video conference data. The UI components are primarily found in `packages/ui-video-conf`, while routing and page logic reside in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference`. The data structures and database interactions are handled by `packages/core-typings` and `packages/models` respectively.

The `packages/ui-video-conf` library provides a set of reusable React components for video conferencing UI. Key components include:
*   `VideoConfPopupContainer` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopup.tsx`): A styled `div` that serves as the visual container for video conference popups, applying consistent styling like box-shadow, background, and borders.
*   `VideoConfPopup` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopup.tsx`): A `forwardRef` React component that wraps its children within the `VideoConfPopupContainer`, providing a standard dialog structure.
*   `VideoConfPopupContent` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopupContent.tsx`): A simple `Box` component used to structure content within the popup, typically as a flex column.
*   `VideoConfPopupSkeleton` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopupSkeleton.tsx`): A loading state component that composes `VideoConfPopup`, `VideoConfPopupHeader`, `VideoConfPopupContent`, and `VideoConfPopupFooter` (the latter two are referenced but not provided in source) using `Skeleton` components from `@rocket.chat/fuselage` to indicate data loading.
*   `VideoConfMessageRow` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfMessage/VideoConfMessageRow.tsx`): A `Box` component designed for displaying content in a row format, often used within messages related to video conferences.

The `VideoConfPopup` component (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopup.tsx`) is the foundational element for displaying video conference-related information in a popup format. It leverages `VideoConfPopupContainer` for its visual styling, including dynamic positioning based on a `position` prop. The `VideoConfPopupSkeleton` (`packages/ui-video-conf/src/VideoConfPopup/VideoConfPopupSkeleton.tsx`) demonstrates how this popup can be used to provide a loading experience. It renders a `VideoConfPopup` and populates its header, content, and footer areas with `Skeleton` placeholders, giving immediate feedback to the user while data is being fetched. This modular approach allows for consistent UI presentation across different video conference contexts, such as within a contextual bar.

The dedicated conference page handles the initiation and display of video calls. The `ConferenceRoute` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferenceRoute.tsx`) serves as the entry point, ensuring user authentication via `AuthenticationCheck` before rendering the `ConferencePage`.

The `ConferencePage` (`apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferencePage.tsx`) is responsible for:
1.  **Query Parameter Extraction**: It retrieves the `callUrl` from `window.location.search`.
2.  **User Context**: It uses `useUserDisplayName` to append the current user's display name to the `callUrl`.
3.  **Call Initiation**: It invokes the `handleOpenCall` function from the `useVideoConfOpenCall` hook (located in `../room/contextualBar/VideoConference/hooks/useVideoConfOpenCall`, though the hook's implementation is not provided) with the prepared `callUrl`.
4.  **Redirection**: After initiating the call, it pushes the user to the 'home' route using `defaultRoute.push()`.
5.  **Error Handling**: If no `callUrl` is found in the query parameters, it renders `ConferencePageError` instead of attempting to open a call.

The `ConferencePageError` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferencePageError.tsx`) displays a user-friendly message indicating that the call was not found and offers a 'Back to login' action if the user is not authenticated.

The system defines specific constants to manage and communicate the availability status of video conference providers. The `availabilityErrors` object (`apps/meteor/lib/videoConference/constants.ts`) contains string identifiers for common issues:
*   `NOT_CONFIGURED`: Indicates that a video conference provider is not set up.
*   `NOT_ACTIVE`: Signifies that a configured provider is not currently active.
*   `NO_APP`: Suggests that no video conference provider application is installed or enabled.
These constants are crucial for consistent error reporting and internal logic related to video conference service provisioning.

The model layer defines the structure and persistence of video conference data.

**Typings (`packages/core-typings/src/IVideoConference.ts`)**:
*   The `IVideoConference` interface is the core data structure, extending `IRocketChatRecord`. It includes properties like `type` (e.g., `'direct'`, `'videoconference'`, `'livechat'`, `'voip'`), `rid` (room ID), `users`, `status`, `url`, `createdBy`, `createdAt`, `endedBy`, `endedAt`, `providerName`, and `providerData`.
*   The `VideoConferenceStatus` enum defines the lifecycle states of a call: `CALLING`, `STARTED`, `EXPIRED`, `ENDED`, `DECLINED`.
*   Specific interfaces like `IDirectVideoConference`, `IGroupVideoConference`, `ILivechatVideoConference`, and `IVoIPVideoConference` extend `IVideoConference` to include type-specific properties (e.g., `title` for group calls, `externalId` for VoIP).
*   Type guards (e.g., `isDirectVideoConference`) are provided for runtime type checking.

**Raw Model (`packages/models/src/models/VideoConference.ts`)**:
*   The `VideoConferenceRaw` class extends `BaseRaw<VideoConference>` and provides direct MongoDB operations for the `video_conference` collection.
*   It defines database indexes on `rid, createdAt`, `type, status`, and `discussionRid` for efficient querying.
*   Methods are available for various CRUD operations:
    *   `findPaginatedByRoomId`, `findAllLongRunning`, `countByTypeAndStatus` for retrieval.
    *   `createDirect`, `createGroup`, `createLivechat`, `createVoIP` for inserting new conference records, each tailored to the specific conference type.
    *   `updateOneById`, `setEndedById`, `setDataById`, `setRingingById`, `setStatusById`, `setUrlById`, `setProviderDataById` for updating specific fields of a video conference record.

DDP Protocol, Realtime Streaming & Publi.text: The Distributed Data Protocol (DDP) is a WebSocket-based protocol used by Rocket.Chat for real-time communication between clients and the server. It enables clients to invoke server-side methods and subscribe to data publications, receiving live updates as data changes. Key DDP message types facilitate this interaction. Outgoing client messages include `sub` for subscriptions and `method` for remote procedure calls, as defined in `packages/ddp-client/src/types/publicationPayloads.ts` and `packages/ddp-client/src/types/methodsPayloads.ts`. Incoming server messages include `ready` and `nosub` for subscription status, `added`, `changed`, `removed` for collection updates, and `result` and `updated` for method call outcomes. These payloads are crucial for maintaining a synchronized state between the client and server, forming the backbone of Rocket.Chat's real-time features.

The client-side interaction with the DDP protocol is encapsulated within the `DDPSDK` class, found in `packages/ddp-client/src/DDPSDK.ts`. This SDK provides a high-level interface for connecting to the Rocket.Chat server and performing DDP operations. To initialize, clients use `DDPSDK.create(url)` or `DDPSDK.createAndConnect(url)` which sets up the core components:

*   `ConnectionImpl`: Manages the WebSocket connection to the DDP server.
*   `DDPDispatcher`: Handles the dispatching of DDP messages (methods, subscriptions) and processing of incoming messages.
*   `ClientStreamImpl`: Implements the `ClientStream` interface (`packages/ddp-client/src/types/ClientStream.ts`), offering methods like `callAsync` for invoking server methods and `subscribe` for publications.
*   `AccountImpl`: Manages user authentication and session tokens.
*   `TimeoutControl`: Handles connection timeouts and pings.
*   `RestClient`: Provides a REST API client, integrating DDP authentication credentials.

The `DDPSDK` exposes `call(method, ...params)` for method invocations and `stream(name, data, cb)` for subscribing to real-time data streams. The `stream` method internally uses `client.subscribe` to a `stream-${name}` publication and `client.onCollection` to listen for `changed` events on that specific collection, filtering by `eventName` to deliver updates to the provided callback.

On the server, the `ddp-streamer` service (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/service.ts`) is responsible for handling DDP connections and managing real-time data streams. It initializes a `Server` instance (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Server.ts`) which acts as the central DDP server, listening for WebSocket connections. Each incoming client connection is represented by a `Client` instance (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Client.ts`), which manages the client's session, subscriptions, and handles incoming DDP messages like `ping`, `method`, and `sub` (from `ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Client.ts`).

The `Server` class provides `methods(obj)` and `publish(name, fn)` to register server-side DDP methods and publications. When a client invokes a method or subscribes to a publication, the `Server` either executes the registered function or, if not found, delegates the call to the `MeteorService` (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Server.ts`) for compatibility with traditional Meteor methods/publications. The `Stream` class (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Streamer.ts`) extends the core `Streamer` module and registers its publications and methods with the `Server`, enabling real-time event broadcasting via `api.broadcast('stream', [name, eventName, args])`.

When a client subscribes to a publication via `ClientStream.subscribe` (client-side) which translates to a `sub` message, the server's `Server.subscribe` method (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Server.ts`) is invoked. This method checks if a publication function is registered for the given name. If found, it instantiates a `Publication` object (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Publication.ts`), passing the `Client` instance and the subscription `packet`.

The `Publication` class represents the server-side lifecycle of a client's subscription. It stores a reference to the `Client` and the `packet.id` in the `client.subscriptions` map. It provides methods like `ready()`, `stop()`, `added(collection, id, fields)`, `changed(collection, id, fields)`, and `removed(collection, id)` which, when called, instruct the `Server` to send the corresponding DDP messages back to the subscribing client. For example, `publication.added('users', 'user123', { name: 'John Doe' })` would result in an `added` DDP message being sent to the client, updating their local `users` collection.

On the client, the `DDPSDK.stream` method (`packages/ddp-client/src/DDPSDK.ts`) is the primary entry point for consuming real-time streams. This method abstracts the DDP subscription mechanism for event-based streaming. It subscribes to a special DDP publication named `stream-${name}` using `this.client.subscribe()`. The `useCollection: false` option indicates that this is not a traditional collection-backed publication but rather a stream of events.

After subscribing, `DDPSDK.stream` registers a listener using `this.client.onCollection(`stream-${name}`, (data) => { ... })`. This listener processes incoming `PublicationPayloads` (`packages/ddp-client/src/types/publicationPayloads.ts`) for the `stream-${name}` collection. It specifically looks for `changed` messages where `data.fields.eventName` matches the `key` provided during the `stream` call. When a match is found, the `cb` callback is invoked with `data.fields.args`, effectively delivering the streamed event data to the client application. While no explicit React integration is shown, this client-side `onCollection` callback is where a React component would typically update its state based on the received real-time data.

The `DDPSDK.stream` method in `packages/ddp-client/src/DDPSDK.ts` exemplifies a 'spotlight' publication pattern, where a single DDP publication (`stream-${name}`) acts as a multiplexer for various real-time events. Instead of creating a separate DDP publication for every distinct event, this pattern uses a generic stream and differentiates events by an `eventName` field within the `changed` payload.

On the server, the `Stream` class (`ee/apps/ddp-streamer/src/Streamer.ts`) facilitates this by registering publications with `server.publish(name, fn)`. When a stream event occurs, the server-side `Stream` can use `changedPayload(collection, id, fields)` to construct a DDP `changed` message. This message is then sent to all relevant subscribers via `sendToManySubscriptions`, where `fields` would contain `eventName` and `args` to be consumed by the client-side `DDPSDK.stream` listener. This approach optimizes DDP usage by reducing the number of active subscriptions while still providing granular real-time updates.

Push Notifications & Notification Queue.text: Push notifications are a critical component of Rocket.Chat, enabling real-time alerts for users on their mobile devices. This system ensures that users are informed of new messages and events even when they are not actively using the application. The process involves constructing notification payloads, dispatching them through various services like Apple Push Notification service (APN) and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM), and managing a queue for reliable delivery.

The Rocket.Chat push notification system orchestrates several key components to deliver alerts. When a message or event triggers a notification, a payload is constructed by the `PushNotification` utility (`apps/meteor/app/push-notifications/server/lib/PushNotification.ts`). This payload is then handed off to the `Push` dispatcher (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/push.ts`), which is responsible for routing the notification to the appropriate external push service (APN or FCM) based on the user's device token. User-specific notification preferences, stored in `ISubscription` documents, heavily influence whether and how a notification is sent. For robustness and asynchronous processing, notifications may be managed through a `NotificationQueue`.

The core of the push notification dispatching logic resides in the `PushClass` (exposed as `Push`) within `apps/meteor/app/push/server/push.ts`. This class manages the configuration and sending of notifications.

*   **Configuration**: The `configure(options: PushOptions)` method initializes the push service, setting parameters like `sendTimeout` and configuring APN (`initAPN`) if `options.apn` is provided. It ensures that configuration happens only once.
*   **Token Management**: The dispatcher interacts with the `PushToken` model (`packages/models/src/index.ts`) to manage device tokens. Methods like `replaceToken(currentToken, newToken)` and `removeToken(token)` handle updates and deletions of tokens.
*   **Gateway Usage**: The `shouldUseGateway()` method determines if notifications should be routed through a push gateway, based on server settings like `Register_Server` and `Cloud_Service_Agree_PrivacyTerms`.
*   **Native Dispatch**: The `sendNotificationNative` method is responsible for sending notifications directly to APN or FCM. It inspects the `IPushToken` type (`apn` or `gcm`) and calls `sendAPN` or `sendFCM` accordingly. The `PendingPushNotification` type (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/definition.ts`) defines the structure of notifications awaiting dispatch.
*   **Logging**: The `logger` (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/logger.ts`) is used to log push-related activities for monitoring and debugging.

The `PushNotification` class (`apps/meteor/app/push-notifications/server/lib/PushNotification.ts`) is responsible for assembling the notification payload before dispatch.

*   **`getNotificationId(roomId)`**: Generates a unique notification ID by hashing the server ID and room ID, ensuring consistent grouping of notifications.
*   **`getNotificationConfig(...)`**: This private method constructs the `IPushNotificationConfig` object. It takes various message and room details, along with user preferences like `idOnly` (controlled by the `Push_request_content_from_server` setting), to determine the notification's title, text, payload, sound, and other platform-specific settings (e.g., `gcm.style`, `apn.category`). The `idOnly` flag dictates whether the full message content is sent or just an identifier, prompting the client to fetch content from the server.
*   **`send(...)`**: This public method is the entry point for sending a notification. It first calls `getNotificationConfig` to build the payload, increments a `metrics.notificationsSent` counter, and then passes the `IPushNotificationConfig` to the `Push.send` method of the push dispatcher.
*   **`getNotificationForMessageId(...)`**: This method prepares a `NotificationPayload` for a specific message. It fetches sender details, applies `beforeSendMessageNotifications` callbacks, handles username replacement for mentions (`replaceMentionedUsernamesWithFullNames`), parses message text per user (`parseMessageTextPerUser`), and uses `getPushData` to gather all necessary information before calling `getNotificationConfig`.

Users can customize their notification preferences for individual rooms through the `saveNotificationSettingsMethod` (`apps/meteor/app/push-notifications/server/methods/saveNotificationSettings.ts`). This Meteor method allows users to control various aspects of notifications:

*   **Configurable Fields**: Users can adjust settings such as `desktopNotifications`, `mobilePushNotifications`, `emailNotifications`, `unreadAlert`, `disableNotifications`, `hideUnreadStatus`, `hideMentionStatus`, `muteGroupMentions`, and `audioNotificationValue`.
*   **Preference Resolution**: The `getNotificationPrefValue` helper determines the effective preference, allowing 'default' values to fall back to server-wide user preferences (`getUserNotificationPreference`).
*   **Persistence**: These settings are stored in the `Subscriptions` collection (`packages/models/src/index.ts`), which holds user-specific configurations for each room. Updates to a subscription trigger `notifyOnSubscriptionChangedById`.

These settings directly influence whether a notification is generated by `PushNotification` and how it is presented to the user.

The Rocket.Chat system includes a `NotificationQueue` to manage the asynchronous dispatch of push notifications. The existence of `INotificationQueueModel` (`packages/models/src/index.ts`) and the `PendingPushNotification` type (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/definition.ts`) strongly indicate its role. A `PendingPushNotification` object, characterized by fields like `sent`, `sending`, `priority`, `createdAt`, and `createdBy`, represents a notification awaiting dispatch.

While the explicit enqueueing and dequeueing logic is not fully detailed in the provided files, the queue serves to:

*   **Decouple Dispatch**: Allow the `PushNotification` payload builder to hand off notifications without waiting for immediate external service responses.
*   **Ensure Reliability**: Facilitate retries and error handling for notifications that fail to send on the first attempt.
*   **Manage Load**: Smooth out bursts of notifications, preventing overwhelming external push services or the Rocket.Chat server itself.

Notifications are likely added to this queue by the `Push` dispatcher, and a background process or internal mechanism then retrieves and processes these `PendingPushNotification` items, ultimately calling the native dispatch methods (`sendAPN`, `sendFCM`).

The journey of a push notification in Rocket.Chat typically follows these steps:

1.  **Message/Event Trigger**: A new message is sent or an event occurs, initiating the notification process.
2.  **Payload Construction**: The `PushNotification` utility (`apps/meteor/app/push-notifications/server/lib/PushNotification.ts`) constructs an `IPushNotificationConfig` payload. This involves fetching sender details, applying callbacks, and considering user notification settings (e.g., `idOnly` from `Push_request_content_from_server`). User-specific preferences stored in `ISubscription` documents (`packages/models/src/index.ts`) are consulted to tailor the notification content and determine if it should be sent.
3.  **Dispatch Request**: The constructed payload is passed to the `Push` dispatcher (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/push.ts`) via `Push.send(config)`.
4.  **Queueing (Implicit)**: The `Push` dispatcher likely enqueues the notification as a `PendingPushNotification` (`apps/meteor/app/push/server/definition.ts`) into the `NotificationQueue` (`packages/models/src/index.ts`) for asynchronous processing.
5.  **Token Retrieval**: When processing a `PendingPushNotification`, the dispatcher retrieves the relevant device `IPushToken` from the `PushToken` collection (`packages/models/src/index.ts`).
6.  **External Service Dispatch**: Based on the `IPushToken` type, the dispatcher calls `sendAPN` for Apple devices or `sendFCM` for Android devices, sending the notification to the respective external push service.
7.  **Device Delivery**: APN or FCM then delivers the notification to the user's mobile device.

Omnichannel Server Engine & Livechat Rou.text: The Omnichannel Server Engine in Rocket.Chat is primarily driven by the `RoutingManager` located at `apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/RoutingManager.ts`. This core component is responsible for orchestrating the entire livechat routing process, from receiving new inquiries to delegating them to available agents. It acts as the central dispatch engine, ensuring that incoming chats are efficiently assigned based on configured routing methods and agent availability. The system is designed to be extensible, allowing different routing strategies to be registered and utilized.

The `RoutingManager` is the heart of livechat routing. It maintains a collection of registered routing `methods` and provides utilities to manage them, such as `isMethodSet()`, `registerMethod(name, Method)`, `getMethod()`, and `getConfig()`. Its primary function is `delegateInquiry(inquiry, agent, options, room)`, which attempts to assign an inquiry to an agent. If an initially suggested `agent` is offline or invalid (checked via `Users.findOneOnlineAgentByUserList` and `allowAgentSkipQueue`), the `RoutingManager` will call `this.getNextAgent(department)` to find an alternative using the currently configured routing method. If no agent is found, the inquiry may remain in a 'ready' state, awaiting manual intervention or future agent availability.

Key operations performed by the `RoutingManager` include:
- `getNextAgent(department, ignoreAgentId)`: Retrieves the next available agent based on the active routing method.
- `unassignAgent(inquiry, departmentId, shouldQueue, agent)`: Removes an agent from an inquiry, potentially requeueing it.
- `takeInquiry(inquiry, agent, options, room)`: Assigns an inquiry to a specific agent.
- `transferRoom(room, guest, transferData)`: Handles the transfer of a livechat room.
- `delegateAgent(agent, inquiry)`: Delegates an inquiry to a specific agent.
- `assignAgent(inquiry, agent)`: Assigns an agent to an inquiry, updating relevant models.

Throughout its operations, the `RoutingManager` interacts heavily with various database models like `LivechatInquiry`, `LivechatRooms`, `Subscriptions`, `Rooms`, and `Users`, and logs its activities using `new Logger('RoutingManager')` from `apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/RoutingManager.ts`.

Rocket.Chat's omnichannel system employs a robust logging infrastructure to provide detailed insights into its operations. Dedicated loggers are instantiated for different components and functionalities. In the core livechat module, `apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/logger.ts` defines:
- `callbackLogger`: For callback-related events.
- `businessHourLogger`: For business hour processing.
- `livechatLogger`: General livechat operations.
- `livechatContactsLogger`: For contact management.
- `webhooksLogger`: For webhook activities.

For enterprise-specific features, `apps/meteor/ee/app/livechat-enterprise/server/lib/logger.ts` extends this with:
- `logger` (LivechatEnterprise): A general logger for enterprise features.
- `queriesLogger`, `helperLogger`, `cbLogger`, `bhLogger`, `contactLogger`: Section-specific loggers for enterprise queries, helpers, callbacks, business hours, and contacts, respectively.
- `schedulerLogger`: For scheduling-related tasks.

Additionally, the `RoutingManager` itself uses `new Logger('RoutingManager')` from `apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/RoutingManager.ts` to log its dispatch and delegation processes, aiding in debugging and monitoring routing decisions.

Rocket.Chat Enterprise introduces several extensions to the omnichannel system, enhancing management and routing capabilities. The `LivechatEnterprise` object in `apps/meteor/ee/app/livechat-enterprise/server/lib/LivechatEnterprise.ts` provides methods for:
- **Monitor Management**: `addMonitor(username)` and `removeMonitor(username)` to assign/revoke the `livechat-monitor` role and manage `LivechatUnitMonitors`.
- **Business Unit Management**: `removeUnit(_id, userId)` and `saveUnit(_id, unitData, unitMonitors, unitDepartments, userId)` for creating, updating, and deleting `LivechatUnit` entities, including their associated monitors and departments.
- **Tag Management**: `removeTag(_id)` and `saveTag(_id, tagData, tagDepartments)` for managing `LivechatTag` objects, which can be used for categorizing chats.
- **SLA Management**: `saveSLA(_id, slaData, executedBy)` for defining and managing `OmnichannelServiceLevelAgreements`.

Furthermore, enterprise features extend core behaviors through patching. The `beforeNewRoomPatched` function in `apps/meteor/ee/app/livechat-enterprise/server/hooks/beforeNewRoom.ts` patches the `beforeNewRoom` hook to automatically associate an SLA with a new omnichannel room if `extraData.sla` is provided. The `isDepartmentCreationAvailablePatch` in `ee/packages/omni-core-ee/src/isDepartmentCreationAvailable.ts` overrides the default `isDepartmentCreationAvailable` from `@rocket.chat/omni-core` to allow unlimited department creation when `License.hasModule('livechat-enterprise')` is active, removing the single-department restriction present in the community edition.

Queue management is implicitly handled by the `RoutingManager`'s `delegateInquiry` method. If no agent is available after attempting to find one via `getNextAgent`, the inquiry remains in a 'ready' state, effectively staying in a queue for manual assignment or when an agent becomes available. This behavior is noted in `apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/RoutingManager.ts`.

Department restrictions are managed through specific functions and enterprise extensions:
- `applyDepartmentRestrictions` from `packages/omni-core/src/hooks/applyDepartmentRestrictions.ts` is a patchable function that allows filtering `ILivechatDepartment` queries based on user permissions or other criteria.
- `isDepartmentCreationAvailable` from `packages/omni-core/src/isDepartmentCreationAvailable.ts` determines if new departments can be created. By default, it returns `true` only if no departments exist (`LivechatDepartment.countTotal() === 0`), enforcing a single-department limit in the community edition.
- The enterprise patch `isDepartmentCreationAvailablePatch` in `ee/packages/omni-core-ee/src/isDepartmentCreationAvailable.ts` overrides this behavior. If `License.hasModule('livechat-enterprise')` is true, it always returns `true`, enabling the creation of multiple departments.

The `packages/livechat/src/lib/api.ts` file provides several utility functions crucial for presenting livechat data through APIs:
- `normalizeAgent(agentData)`: Takes raw agent data and returns a simplified object with `name`, `username`, and `status`, suitable for external consumption.
- `normalizeQueueAlert(queueInfo)`: Processes queue information (like `spot` and `estimatedWaitTimeSeconds`) to generate a user-friendly, localized message about the visitor's position and estimated wait time in the queue. It dynamically imports `date-fns/formatDistance` and uses `i18next` for internationalization.

Additionally, `packages/livechat/src/lib/email.ts` offers email validation utilities:
- `validateEmail(email, options)`: Provides two styles of email validation: `'basic'` (a simple regex check) and `'rfc'` (a more comprehensive RFC-compliant regex check), ensuring email addresses meet specified formats.

The `IOmnichannelTranscriptService` interface, defined in `packages/core-services/src/types/IOmnichannelTranscriptService.ts`, outlines the contract for services responsible for handling livechat transcripts. This interface currently specifies one method:
- `workOnPdf({ details })`: Takes `WorkDetailsWithSource` (which includes `rid` for the room ID, `userId` for the user ID, and `from` indicating the source of the request) and is responsible for processing and generating a PDF transcript of the livechat conversation. This service is crucial for post-chat operations, allowing users to obtain a record of their interactions.

The omnichannel server engine orchestrates the journey of a livechat inquiry. When a new inquiry arrives, the `RoutingManager` (`apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/RoutingManager.ts`) takes charge. It consults the currently configured routing `method` to determine the best course of action for `agent_selection`. This selection process can be heavily influenced by `enterprise_features` (e.g., Service Level Agreements, Business Units, Monitors) and `department_rules` (`packages/omni-core/src/hooks/applyDepartmentRestrictions.ts`, `packages/omni-core/src/isDepartmentCreationAvailable.ts`). The `RoutingManager` interacts with `livechat_models` (e.g., `LivechatInquiry`, `LivechatRooms`, `Users`) to update inquiry statuses, assign agents, and manage room subscriptions. All these operations are meticulously recorded by the `logging_infra` (`apps/meteor/app/livechat/server/lib/logger.ts`, `apps/meteor/ee/app/livechat-enterprise/server/lib/logger.ts`). For external interactions, `api_utils` (`packages/livechat/src/lib/api.ts`) normalize data and provide user-friendly alerts. Post-chat, the `transcript_service` (`packages/core-services/src/types/IOmnichannelTranscriptService.ts`) can generate records like PDF transcripts based on data from `livechat_models`.

Livechat Embedded Widget.text: The Livechat Embedded Widget provides a client-side interface for interacting with Rocket.Chat's livechat functionality. It's designed to be embedded into any webpage, allowing visitors to initiate and manage chat sessions. The widget handles API communication, state management, UI rendering, and communication with its parent window, ensuring a seamless user experience. Its core components manage visitor identity, chat configuration, message display, and interactive UI elements powered by UI Kit.

The widget establishes its connection to the Rocket.Chat server using an API client defined in `packages/livechat/src/api.ts`. The `Livechat` client is an instance created from `@rocket.chat/ddp-client`'s `LivechatClientImpl.create`. The server host is determined dynamically, prioritizing `window.SERVER_URL`, then a `serverUrl` query parameter from `window.location.search`, and defaulting to `http://localhost:3000` in development. SSL usage is detected by checking if the resolved host matches `^https:` via the `useSsl` boolean. The client also includes a REST interceptor (`Livechat.rest.use`) to catch and parse JSON errors from `Response` objects, re-throwing them for consistent error handling.

Centralized state management for the Livechat widget is handled by a `Store` instance, initialized in `packages/livechat/src/store/index.tsx`. The `StoreState` type defines the comprehensive structure of the application's state, including `token`, `config` (messages, theme, settings, triggers, departments), `messages`, `user` (visitor data), `iframe` properties, `gdpr` consent status, and UI states like `visible` and `minimized`. The `initialState()` function provides default values, and the `dontPersist` array specifies keys that should not be persisted across sessions. A unique `sessionId` is generated using `createToken()` from `../lib/random.ts` and stored in `sessionStorage` upon window load. Event listeners for `load`, `visibilitychange`, and `beforeunload` manage the `openSessionIds` in the store and trigger `parentCall` actions based on widget visibility and minimization status.

The Livechat widget communicates with its embedding parent window or opener using the `parentCall` utility function defined in `packages/livechat/src/lib/parentCall.ts`. This function first identifies the target window using `getParentWindowTarget()`, preferring `window.opener` if available and not closed, otherwise falling back to `window.parent`. It then sends a message via `postMessage`, encapsulating the method name (`fn`), arguments (`args`), and a `src: 'rocketchat'` identifier within a data object. The `runCallbackEventEmitter` function further leverages `parentCall` to dispatch specific callbacks (e.g., `callbackName`) to the parent window, but only if the `callbackName` is included in the `VALID_CALLBACKS` list (defined in `../widget`, not provided in source).

Various randomness utilities are provided in `packages/livechat/src/lib/random.ts`, which wrap functionality from the `@rocket.chat/random` package. These helpers include `chooseElement` (for selecting a random element from an array), `createRandomString` (for generating a random string), `createRandomId` (for generating a unique ID), and `createToken` (specifically for generating a 64-character hexadecimal string, used for session tokens and visitor tokens). These functions ensure the generation of unique identifiers and random selections throughout the widget's operation.

The widget utilizes UI Kit for rendering interactive message blocks. The fundamental `Block` type, defined in `packages/ui-kit/src/blocks/Block.ts`, serves as a union of `TextObject`, `BlockElement`, and `LayoutBlock`. The rendering process involves a `Surface` component (`packages/livechat/src/components/uiKit/message/Surface.tsx`) which provides a `SurfaceContext` containing a `dispatchAction` function. Child components can access this dispatcher via the `useDispatchAction` hook. The `Block` component (`packages/livechat/src/components/uiKit/message/Block.tsx`) further provides a `BlockContext` with `appId` and `blockId`. The `usePerformAction` hook, used within UI Kit elements, leverages this context to dispatch actions associated with specific `actionId`s and `appId`s, managing a `performing` state during the asynchronous action execution.

For displaying text content, the widget employs specialized components that handle markdown and emoji rendering. The `PlainText` component (`packages/livechat/src/components/uiKit/message/PlainText/index.tsx`) and `Mrkdwn` component (`packages/livechat/src/components/uiKit/message/Mrkdwn/index.tsx`) both serve this purpose. Both components preprocess their input `text` using `shortnameToUnicode` from `../../../lib/emoji/shortnameToUnicode` to convert emoji shortcodes (e.g., `:smile:`) into their Unicode equivalents. The processed text is then passed to a `MarkdownBlock` component for rendering, with `Mrkdwn` explicitly enabling `emoticons` support.

The message list in the Livechat widget is composed of several specialized UI components. `MessageTime` (`packages/livechat/src/components/Messages/MessageTime/index.tsx`) is responsible for formatting and displaying message timestamps, using `date-fns` (`parseISO`, `isToday`) for date logic and `react-i18next`'s `withTranslation` for localization. `MessageSeparator` (`packages/livechat/src/components/Messages/MessageSeparator/index.tsx`) renders visual separators in the message list, displaying either a formatted date or an 'unread messages' indicator, also leveraging `withTranslation`. `AudioAttachment` (`packages/livechat/src/components/Messages/AudioAttachment/index.tsx`) displays audio files, embedding an `<audio>` HTML element within a `MessageBubble` and providing a localized fallback message. All these components utilize the `createClassName` helper from `../../../helpers/createClassName` for consistent styling.

Matrix Federation & Cross-Server Messagi.text: Rocket.Chat's Matrix Federation implementation enables secure cross-server communication, allowing users on different Rocket.Chat instances (or other Matrix-compatible servers) to interact within federated rooms and exchange media. This system ensures that actions within federated rooms, such as user management or room setting changes, are subject to specific authorization rules, and all incoming requests from remote servers are authenticated and authorized. The core functionality relies on the `@rocket.chat/federation-sdk` for cryptographic verification and interaction with external Matrix servers.

The federation system in Rocket.Chat is composed of several key parts. On the server-side, dedicated API routes are registered to handle incoming federation requests from remote Matrix servers, protected by authentication and authorization middlewares (`ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/api/middlewares/isAuthenticated.ts`, `ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/api/middlewares/canAccessResource.ts`). Media handling, including local storage and remote downloading, is managed by the `MatrixMediaService` (`ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/services/MatrixMediaService.ts`). Client-side logic (`apps/meteor/client/lib/federation/Federation.ts`) ensures that user actions and room settings adhere to federation-specific rules. The overall system can be enabled or disabled via a server setting, checked by `isFederationEnabled()` (`apps/meteor/server/services/federation/utils.ts`).

Client-side authorization for federated rooms is handled by `apps/meteor/client/lib/federation/Federation.ts`. The `actionAllowed` function determines if a specific `RoomMemberActions` (e.g., `REMOVE_USER`, `BAN`, `SET_AS_OWNER`, `SET_AS_MODERATOR`) is permitted for a user in a federated room. This function checks if the room `isRoomFederated` and not a direct message, and then evaluates the `loggedInUserRoomRoles` (owner, moderator) against the `displayingUserRoomRoles` to enforce permissions. For instance, owners can set other users as owners/moderators or remove/ban non-owners. Similarly, `isEditableByTheUser` checks if a user (owner or moderator) can edit a federated room, and `canCreateInviteLinks` specifically allows owners/moderators in *public* federated rooms to create invite links. The `isRoomSettingAllowed` function restricts changes to `RoomSettingsEnum.NAME` and `RoomSettingsEnum.TOPIC` for federated rooms, preventing modifications to other settings.

Federation API endpoints are secured by authentication and authorization middlewares defined in `ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/api/middlewares`. The `isAuthenticatedMiddleware` verifies incoming requests from remote Matrix servers. It extracts the `Authorization` header, HTTP `method`, `path`, and request `body`, then uses `federationSDK.verifyRequestSignature(authHeader, method, path, body)` to validate the request's signature. If verification fails, it returns an `M_UNAUTHORIZED` error. Upon successful verification, the `authenticatedServer` information is stored in the Hono context (`c.set('authenticatedServer')`) for subsequent use. Building upon this, `canAccessResourceMiddleware(entityType)` (from `ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/api/middlewares/canAccessResource.ts`) ensures that the authenticated server has permission to access a specific `event`, `media`, or `room` resource by calling `federationSDK.canAccessResource(entityType, resourceId, c.get('authenticatedServer'))`. This middleware combines `isAuthenticatedMiddleware` with the resource access check using `every(isAuthenticatedMiddleware(), canAccessResource(entityType))`.

The `MatrixMediaService` (`ee/packages/federation-matrix/src/services/MatrixMediaService.ts`) is responsible for handling media files in federated contexts. It provides static methods like `generateMXCUri(fileId, serverName)` to create Matrix Content URIs (e.g., `mxc://serverName/fileId`) and `parseMXCUri(mxcUri)` to extract server name and media ID. When preparing a local file for Matrix, `prepareLocalFileForMatrix(fileId, serverName, matrixRoomId)` retrieves the file from `Uploads` and updates its `federation` info with the generated MXC URI. To retrieve a local file, `getLocalFileForMatrixNode(mediaId, serverName)` first checks `Avatars` by `etag` and then `Uploads` by `federation.mediaId` and `federation.serverName`, or by `_id`.
