For more specialized or high-volume background tasks, the `queue-worker` microservice (`ee/apps/queue-worker`) is deployed, which can host various worker implementations, such as the `QueueWorker` from `@rocket.chat/omnichannel-services`.

The `Agenda` class (`packages/agenda/src/Agenda.ts`) is the central component of the job scheduling system. It extends `EventEmitter` and connects to a MongoDB instance to store and manage jobs. Key configurations include `name`, `processEvery` (how often to scan for new jobs, using `human-interval`), `defaultConcurrency`, `maxConcurrency`, `defaultLockLimit`, `lockLimit`, and `defaultLockLifetime`.

Jobs are represented by the `Job` class (`packages/agenda/src/Job.ts`), which encapsulates job attributes (`IJobAttributes` from `packages/agenda/src/definition/IJob.ts`) such as `name`, `nextRunAt`, `repeatInterval`, `repeatAt`, `priority`, and `data`. The `Job` class provides methods like `computeNextRunAt()` to determine the next execution time. This computation can use `CronTime` for cron-style intervals or `human-interval` for human-readable durations, and `date.js` for specific `repeatAt` times. Jobs are created using the `createJob` function (`packages/agenda/src/createJob.ts`). `Agenda` manages the lifecycle of jobs, including locking (`_lockedJobs`), running (`_runningJobs`), and queuing (`_jobQueue`) them for processing.

The `@rocket.chat/cron` package (`packages/cron/src/index.ts`) provides the `AgendaCronJobs` class, which simplifies the interaction with the `Agenda` core library for common cron job patterns. Upon `start()`, it initializes an `Agenda` instance, connecting to MongoDB using the `rocketchat_cron` collection for job definitions. It sets up comprehensive event listeners for `start`, `complete`, `success`, `fail`, and `error` events, logging job lifecycle and potential issues using `@rocket.chat/logger`.

The `AgendaCronJobs` class offers `add()` to schedule recurring jobs (using `scheduler.every()`) and `addAtTimestamp()` for one-time scheduled tasks (using `scheduler.schedule()`). The `define()` method registers the actual job callback function with Agenda. A crucial aspect is the `runCronJobFunctionAndPersistResult()` utility, which wraps job execution to automatically record `intendedAt`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, and `result` (or `error`) in the `CronHistory` collection (`@rocket.chat/models`). This ensures a persistent audit trail for all scheduled cron jobs.

The `queue-worker` microservice (`ee/apps/queue-worker/src/service.ts`) is a dedicated application designed to handle background tasks, particularly in an enterprise context. It initializes a MongoDB connection (`getConnection`), sets up distributed tracing (`startTracing`), and registers service models (`registerServiceModels`). It integrates with the `@rocket.chat/network-broker` to facilitate inter-service communication. The service then imports and registers specific worker implementations, such as the `QueueWorker` from `@rocket.chat/omnichannel-services`, with the core API (`api.registerService`). Once all services are registered and started (`api.start()`), the `queue-worker` exposes a `/health` endpoint via `polka` to allow for health checks, ensuring its operational status.

Job Scheduling, Agenda & Queue Worker.section: Presence Reaping as a Representative Consumer
Job Scheduling, Agenda & Queue Worker.text:
The `PresenceReaper` class (`ee/packages/presence/src/lib/PresenceReaper.ts`) serves as a concrete example of a background worker that performs periodic maintenance. It is not directly managed by `Agenda` or `AgendaCronJobs` in the provided code, but rather uses Node.js's native `setInterval` to schedule its `run()` method every minute. The `PresenceReaper` is responsible for identifying and removing stale user connections from the `UsersSessions` collection (`@rocket.chat/models`).

During its `run()` cycle, it calculates a `cutoffDate` and queries `UsersSessions` for connections older than this threshold. It then processes these documents, identifies stale connections for each user (`processDocument`), and performs a `bulkWrite` operation to `$pull` these connections from the database (`flushBatch`). After updating the database, it invokes an `onUpdate` callback, notifying other parts of the system about the users whose presence status might have changed due to connection reaping. This demonstrates a common pattern for workers: periodic data cleanup and state synchronization.

Microservice Network & Authorization Ser.text: Rocket.Chat's microservice architecture relies on a robust network for inter-service communication and a dedicated authorization service to manage access control. The `packages/core-services/src/index.ts` file serves as a central hub, exporting various service interfaces (e.g., `IAccount`, `IAuthorization`) and utilities for service orchestration. Communication between services is facilitated by a network broker, which is initialized and managed by components like the `queue-worker` service, ensuring that different parts of the application can interact seamlessly and securely.

The motivation behind this microservice architecture is to enhance scalability, maintainability, and allow for independent deployment of different functionalities. Core service interfaces, such as `IAccount` for user account management and `IAuthorization` for access control, are defined in `packages/core-services/src/index.ts` and its associated `types` directory. These interfaces establish clear contracts for how services should behave and interact. Services are typically implemented using `ServiceClass` or `ServiceClassInternal` (exported from `packages/core-services/src/types/ServiceClass.ts`), providing a standardized way to build and integrate new functionalities into the Rocket.Chat ecosystem.

The Account Service manages user sessions, from creation to expiration. When a user logs in, a new login token is generated using `_generateStampedLoginToken` in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts`, which produces an `IStampedToken` containing a `token` (UUID) and a `when` timestamp. This token is then hashed by `_hashLoginToken` (also in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts`) and transformed into an `IHashedStampedToken` by `_hashStampedToken`. The `saveSession` function in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/saveSession.ts` persists this `hashedToken` by pushing it into the `services.resume.loginTokens` array of the user's document in the `Users` collection.

For session resumption, the `loginViaResume` function in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/loginViaResume.ts` takes a resume token, hashes it using `_hashLoginToken`, and queries the `Users` collection for a matching `hashedToken`. It then checks the token's expiration using `_tokenExpiration` (from `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts`), throwing a `MeteorError` if expired. To log out or invalidate a session, `removeSession` in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/removeSession.ts` removes the corresponding token from the user's `services.resume.loginTokens` array in the `Users` collection.

REST API authentication is defined through specific typings and schemas to ensure consistent request and response structures. The `packages/rest-typings/src/v1/auth.ts` file defines `AuthEndpoints`, which specify the `/v1/login` and `/v1/logout` endpoints. The `LoginProps` type outlines the expected parameters for a login request, which can include `email`, `username`, `user` (an object containing `username` or `email`), `password` (which can be a `string` or an object `{ hashed: string }`), and an optional `code`. Validation for these properties is handled by `isLoginProps`, which is an `ajv` compiled schema, ensuring that incoming requests conform to the defined structure.

Secure handling of authentication tokens is critical, and Rocket.Chat employs specific hashing utilities for this purpose. The `_hashLoginToken` function in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts` and the `hashLoginToken` function in `packages/account-utils/src/index.ts` both perform SHA256 hashing on login tokens, converting them to a base64 digest. This ensures that raw tokens are never stored directly. The `_hashStampedToken` utility in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts` further processes an `IStampedToken` by hashing its `token` property and returning an `IHashedStampedToken` object, preserving other metadata. For user passwords, `getPassword` in `ee/apps/account-service/src/lib/utils.ts` handles SHA256 hashing for plain string passwords or extracts a pre-digested hash. Password validation against bcrypt hashes is performed by `validatePassword` using `bcrypt.compare`.

Authorization within Rocket.Chat is managed through dedicated services that adhere to defined interfaces. The `IAuthorization` and `IAuthorizationLivechat` types, along with `RoomAccessValidator`, are exported from `packages/core-services/src/index.ts` (originating from `packages/core-services/src/types/IAuthorization.ts` and `packages/core-services/src/types/IAuthorizationLivechat.ts`). These interfaces define the contract for authorization services, allowing them to determine user permissions and access rights. Additionally, `IAbacService` (from `packages/core-services/src/types/IAbacService.ts`) provides an interface for Attribute-Based Access Control, enabling fine-grained permission management. Services interact with the authorization system by calling methods exposed through the `api` object (exported by `packages/core-services/src/index.ts`), which acts as a proxy to the actual service implementations.

Services in Rocket.Chat are bootstrapped and orchestrated through a standardized process. The `ServiceStarter` (exported from `packages/core-services/src/index.ts`) plays a role in this. A clear example of service orchestration is found in the `queue-worker` service (`ee/apps/queue-worker/src/service.ts`). This service first establishes a MongoDB connection using `getConnection` and initializes tracing with `startTracing`. It then registers service models via `registerServiceModels`. Crucially, it starts the `network-broker` using `startBroker` (from `@rocket.chat/network-broker`) and sets this broker on the `api` object (from `@rocket.chat/core-services`). After importing and instantiating the `QueueWorker` service, it registers it with `api.registerService` and finally starts all registered services using `api.start()`. The `queue-worker` also exposes a `/health` endpoint via `polka` to monitor its operational status, demonstrating a typical service lifecycle.

The data flow for authentication and authorization typically begins with a user interacting with the REST API endpoints (e.g., `/v1/login`). These requests are routed to the `Account Service`, which then utilizes `Token Hashing Utilities` to generate and hash session tokens. These hashed tokens are securely stored in the `Users Collection` within MongoDB. For subsequent requests, the `Account Service` retrieves and validates these tokens from the `Users Collection` to authenticate the user. Other microservices communicate with each other via the `Network Broker`, leveraging the interfaces defined by `Core Services API`. The `Authorization Service`, also interacting through the `Core Services API` and potentially querying the `Users Collection` for user roles and permissions, is responsible for evaluating access rights for various operations across the application.

Client SDK, API Client & Shared Utilitie.section: Client SDK, API Client & Shared Utilities
Client SDK, API Client & Shared Utilitie.text: The `packages/api-client` module provides the core `RestClient` for interacting with the Rocket.Chat REST API. It defines a `RestClientInterface` (`packages/api-client/src/RestClientInterface.ts`) that outlines standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and specialized operations like `upload`. This module also includes types for `Credentials` (`packages/api-client/src/Credentials.ts`) and specific error discriminators for Two-Factor Authentication. Beyond the API client, the codebase includes various shared utilities, constants, and error classes spread across `apps/meteor` and `packages/ui-client`, facilitating consistent application-wide behavior.

The `RestClientInterface` (`packages/api-client/src/RestClientInterface.ts`) is a TypeScript interface that defines the contract for making HTTP requests to the Rocket.Chat REST API. It includes overloaded methods for `get`, `post`, `put`, and `delete` operations, supporting both endpoints with and without parameters, and returning `Promise<Serialized<OperationResult>>`. A dedicated `upload` method is provided for file uploads, returning an `XMLHttpRequest` and allowing progress event handling. The interface also specifies methods for `getCredentials`, `setCredentials`, and a `use` method for applying `Middleware` to the `send` operation. The `RestClient` class (`packages/api-client/src/index.ts`) implements this interface, handling details like query parameter stringification, JSON body serialization, and `FormData` construction for file uploads via `buildFormData` and `checkIfIsFormData`.

Credential management within the `RestClient` is handled through the `Credentials` type (`packages/api-client/src/Credentials.ts`), which expects `X-User-Id` and `X-Auth-Token` headers. The `RestClientInterface` (`packages/api-client/src/RestClientInterface.ts`) defines `getCredentials()` and `setCredentials()` methods. The `RestClient` class (`packages/api-client/src/index.ts`) stores these credentials internally and applies them to outgoing requests. The `setCredentials` method allows updating the authentication tokens, ensuring subsequent API calls are properly authenticated.

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) error handling is supported by specific error discriminators. The `packages/api-client/src/errors.ts` file provides functions like `isTotpRequiredError`, `isTotpInvalidError`, `isTwoFactorMethod`, and `hasRequiredTwoFactorMethod` to identify 2FA-related errors from API responses. The `RestClientInterface` (`packages/api-client/src/RestClientInterface.ts`) includes a `handleTwoFactorChallenge` method, allowing the client to provide a callback for handling 2FA prompts. Similarly, `apps/meteor/client/lib/2fa/utils.ts` contains analogous discriminators such as `isTotpRequiredError`, `isTotpInvalidError`, and `isTotpMaxAttemptsError`, which are specifically typed for `Meteor.Error` objects, indicating a client-side utility for Meteor applications.

Application-wide external links are registered in dedicated files. Both `apps/meteor/client/lib/links.ts` and `packages/ui-client/src/lib/links.ts` define a `links` object, prefixed by `GO_ROCKET_CHAT_PREFIX` (`https://go.rocket.chat`). These registries contain a comprehensive list of URLs for documentation, apps, support, and marketing pages. Notably, the content of these two files is largely duplicated, providing a centralized, albeit redundant, source for navigating to Rocket.Chat's external resources. Many entries are also marked as `@deprecated`, advising the use of `go.rocket.chat` links.

Various application-wide constants are defined to ensure consistent behavior and styling. For instance, `apps/meteor/lib/constants.ts` defines `NOTIFICATION_ATTACHMENT_COLOR` for UI consistency and `MAX_MULTIPLE_UPLOADED_FILES` to enforce limits on file uploads. These constants are used across different parts of the application to maintain uniformity.

The codebase includes several specialized error classes for specific domains. `apps/meteor/lib/errors/CloudWorkspaceConnectionError.ts` defines `CloudWorkspaceConnectionError`, which extends `CloudWorkspaceError` (an implicit base class not provided in the source). For Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), `ee/packages/abac/src/errors.ts` introduces an `AbacErrorCode` enum and a base `AbacError` class, along with numerous specific error types such as `AbacInvalidAttributeValuesError`, `AbacAttributeNotFoundError`, and `AbacRoomNotFoundError`. These structured error classes facilitate precise error handling and reporting within their respective features.

A collection of utility functions provides common helpers. In `apps/meteor/lib`, `getUserEmailAddress` (`apps/meteor/lib/getUserEmailAddress.ts`) extracts an email address from a user object, while `getUserDisplayNames` (`apps/meteor/lib/getUserDisplayNames.ts`) generates an array of display names (real name and/or username) for a user, utilizing `normalizeUsername`. The `packages/api-client/src/index.ts` also contains utilities like `pipe` for function composition, `buildFormData` for constructing `FormData` objects, and `checkIfIsFormData` for detecting file uploads within parameters.

Crypto, Random & General-Purpose Package.text: This section introduces a collection of utility packages within the Rocket.Chat codebase, designed to handle cryptographic operations, random number generation, data encoding, general-purpose tooling, and specialized communication protocols. These packages provide foundational functionalities for secure operations, data manipulation, and integration with external services and desktop environments.

The `pkg:random` package is intended for generating random numbers. While the specific implementation details are not provided in the current source files, its `jest.config.ts` (`packages/random/jest.config.ts`) indicates separate test configurations for client and server environments, suggesting it provides utilities for both.

The `pkg:sha256` package provides utilities for SHA-256 hashing. A key component is the `binb2hex` function, defined in `packages/sha256/src/binb2hex.ts`. This function takes a binary array (`ArrayLike<number>`) and converts it into a hexadecimal string representation. This conversion is typically used to format the output of a cryptographic hash function into a human-readable or standard hexadecimal format. The package's `jest.config.ts` (`packages/sha256/jest.config.ts`) confirms its server-side nature.

The `pkg:base64` package is responsible for Base64 encoding and decoding operations. Similar to `pkg:random`, the provided source files only include its `jest.config.ts` (`packages/base64/jest.config.ts`), which indicates it's a server-side package. The actual encoding/decoding logic is not present in the provided snippets.

The `pkg:tools` package offers a variety of general-purpose utilities:
  • **Stream Conversion**: The `streamToBuffer` function in `packages/tools/src/stream.ts` converts a Node.js `Readable` stream into a `Promise`. It accumulates data chunks and resolves with the concatenated buffer upon stream completion or rejects on error.
  • **Type Conversion**: The `convertFromDaysToMilliseconds` function in `packages/tools/src/converter.ts` provides a utility to convert a number of days into its equivalent value in milliseconds, ensuring the input is a valid integer.
  • **Type Guards**: The `isRecord` function in `packages/tools/src/isRecord.ts` acts as a type guard, checking if an `unknown` value is a plain JavaScript object (a record) and not an array or null. This is useful for runtime type assertions.
The package's `jest.config.ts` (`packages/tools/jest.config.ts`) confirms its server-side usage.

This group of packages handles authentication, authorization, and server-side data fetching:
  • **JWT (`pkg:jwt`)**: This package is designed for working with JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), typically for authentication and secure information exchange. Its `jest.config.ts` (`packages/jwt/jest.config.ts`) indicates it's a server-side utility.
  • **CAS Validation (`pkg:cas-validate`)**: This package provides functionalities for validating credentials against a Central Authentication Service (CAS). Its `jest.config.ts` (`packages/cas-validate/jest.config.ts`) confirms its server-side nature.
  • **Server Fetch (`pkg:server-fetch`)**: This package extends standard `fetch` capabilities for server-side operations. The `packages/server-fetch/src/types.ts` file defines `ExtendedFetchOptions`, which includes additional parameters like `compress`, `follow`, `size`, `timeout`, `params`, and crucial Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) validation options (`ignoreSsrfValidation` and `allowList`). This indicates that `pkg:server-fetch` provides a robust and secure way to make HTTP requests from the server.

These packages facilitate communication between the Rocket.Chat server and cloud services, and provide an API for desktop application integration:
  • **Server-Cloud Communication (`pkg:server-cloud-communication`)**: This package is intended for managing communication between the Rocket.Chat server and external cloud services. No specific implementation files were provided, but its purpose is to handle this critical integration.
  • **Desktop API (`pkg:desktop-api`)**: This package defines the `IRocketChatDesktop` interface in `packages/desktop-api/src/index.ts`, which serves as the primary interface for the Rocket.Chat desktop application to interact with the underlying operating system and provide enhanced user experiences. Key functionalities exposed include:
    • **Notifications**: `dispatchCustomNotification` and `createNotification` for sending custom and standard desktop notifications.
    • **Server Information & URL Handling**: `onReady`, `setServerInfo`, and `setUrlResolver` for managing server connection status and URL resolution.
    • **UI Management**: `setBadge`, `setFavicon`, `setBackground`, `setSidebarCustomTheme`, `setTitle`, and `setUserThemeAppearance` for controlling various aspects of the desktop application's user interface.
    • **User Presence & Authentication**: `setUserLoggedIn`, `setUserPresenceDetection`, and `setUserToken` for managing user login state, presence, and authentication tokens.
    • **System Integration**: `writeTextToClipboard` for clipboard operations, `openInternalVideoChatWindow` for video chat, `openDocumentViewer` for document viewing, and `getOutlookEvents`, `setOutlookExchangeUrl`, `hasOutlookCredentials`, `clearOutlookCredentials` for Outlook calendar integration.
    • **Application Control**: `reloadServer` for reloading the server connection.

Custom Meteor Packages & Legacy Infrastr.text: Rocket.Chat leverages a set of custom Meteor packages to extend and modify the default Meteor framework behavior, addressing specific application needs and integrating with existing infrastructure. These packages often provide build-time transformations, server-side HTML injection, client-side update mechanisms, and database interaction utilities, forming a crucial part of the application's architecture.

The `autoupdate` package manages client-side updates and hot reloads. On the server, `apps/meteor/packages/autoupdate/autoupdate_server.js` publishes the `meteor_autoupdate_clientVersions` collection, which contains version hashes for different client architectures (e.g., `web.browser`, `web.cordova`). These versions include `version`, `versionRefreshable` (for CSS), `versionNonRefreshable` (for HTML/JS), and `versionReplaceable` (for HMR). The `AUTOUPDATE_VERSION` environment variable can override these calculated hashes. The server uses `WebApp.calculateClientHash` and `WebAppInternals.generateBoilerplate` to determine these versions and assets, updating the `ClientVersions` collection via `WebApp.onListening`.

On the client, `apps/meteor/packages/autoupdate/autoupdate_client.js` subscribes to this collection. It uses `Autoupdate.newClientAvailable()` as a reactive data source to detect new versions. If `versionNonRefreshable` changes, it triggers a "hard code push" causing a full page reload (after a delay in production). If only `versionRefreshable` changes, it performs a "soft code push" by dynamically swapping CSS `<link>` tags without a full reload. Subscription failures are handled by `Autoupdate._retrySubscription`.

The `rocketchat:version` package, defined in `apps/meteor/packages/rocketchat-version/package.js`, registers a build plugin named `compileVersion`. This plugin, implemented in `apps/meteor/packages/rocketchat-version/plugin/compile-version.js`, processes `.info` files during the build process to inject critical version and build-time metadata into the application's JavaScript bundle.

For `rocketchat.info` files, the `VersionCompiler` reads the application version and `minimumClientVersions` from `package.json`. It then gathers extensive build information, including the build date, Node.js version, OS details, and CPU count. Furthermore, it queries the Git repository using `git log` and `git describe` to inject the current commit hash, date, author, subject, tag, and branch. This data is then exposed as `exports.Info` and `exports.minimumClientVersions` in the generated JavaScript.

For `rocketchat-supported-versions.info` files, the compiler fetches supported server versions from the Rocket.Chat release API (`https://releases.rocket.chat/v2/server/supportedVersions`). It validates the response's timestamp and expiration dates before injecting the data as `exports.supportedVersions`.

The `meteor-inject-initial` package provides a mechanism to inject dynamic content into the HTML served by Meteor on the server-side. This is achieved by hijacking the HTTP response stream. The `Inject` object, defined in `apps/meteor/packages/meteor-inject-initial/lib/inject-server.js`, offers methods like `Inject.obj()`, `Inject.meta()`, `Inject.rawHead()`, and `Inject.rawBody()` to queue data or raw HTML for injection into `<script type='application/ejson'>`, `<meta>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags, respectively. It also supports `Inject.rawModHtml()` for custom HTML transformation functions.

The core of this functionality lies in `apps/meteor/packages/meteor-inject-initial/lib/inject-core.js`, where `Inject._hijackWrite(res)` overrides the `res.write` method of the Node.js HTTP response object. This allows the package to intercept the initial HTML chunk (identified by `<!DOCTYPE html>`) before it's sent to the client. The hijacked `write` method then iterates through registered `Inject.rawModHtmlFuncs` (which include `_injectObjects`, `_injectMeta`, `_injectHeads`, `_injectBodies`) to apply all queued modifications to the HTML. This middleware is registered globally using `WebApp.connectHandlers.use`.

The `meteor-run-as-user` package includes a critical patch for a known issue in Meteor 3.0 related to Minimongo collection operations. Specifically, `apps/meteor/packages/meteor-run-as-user/lib/collection.overwrites.js` overwrites the `_eachPossiblyMatchingDocAsync` and `_eachPossiblyMatchingDocSync` methods on `LocalCollection.prototype`. This fix addresses a bug where `MinimongoCollection.remove(query)` with a `$in` operator for `_id` would incorrectly remove only the first matching record instead of all of them. The overwrite modifies the condition from `!fn(doc,id)` to `(await fn(doc, id)) === false` (for async) and `fn(doc, id) === false` (for sync) to ensure correct iteration and removal behavior.

The `rocketchat-postcss` package, defined by `apps/meteor/packages/rocketchat-postcss/build.js`, integrates PostCSS into Meteor's CSS build pipeline. It registers a minifier plugin for `.css` files. The plugin first asynchronously loads the `postcss.config.js` configuration using `postcssrc`, retrieving plugins, a custom parser, and a list of `excludedPackages`.

During processing, it filters out CSS files marked as imports (e.g., `.import.css` or those in `imports/` directories) and files belonging to `excludedPackages`. For the remaining CSS files, `getAbstractSyntaxTree` processes their content: if a file is excluded, `CssTools.parseCss` is used directly; otherwise, `postcss(postcssConfigPlugins).process` applies the configured PostCSS transformations. Errors, including `CssSyntaxError`, are reported via `file.error()`.

The `mergeCssFiles` function then combines the Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) of all processed CSS files using `CssTools.mergeCssAsts`. It then uses `CssTools.stringifyCss` to generate the final CSS code and a source map. Source maps from individual files are merged using `SourceMapConsumer` and `SourceMapGenerator`. Finally, `processFilesForBundle` adds the merged CSS to the bundle. In development mode, the raw merged CSS is added; in production, `CssTools.minifyCssAsync` is used to minify the CSS before adding it to the bundle.

The `packages/models/src/updater.ts` file introduces the `UpdaterImpl<T>` class, which provides a structured and type-safe way to construct MongoDB update filters for Rocket.Chat's data models. This class implements the `Updater<T>` interface and offers methods corresponding to common MongoDB update operators: `set()`, `unset()`, `inc()`, and `addToSet()`. Internally, it maintains `Map` and `Set` objects (`_set`, `_unset`, `_inc`, `_addToSet`) to accumulate the desired changes.

The `getRawUpdateFilter()` method compiles these accumulated changes into a standard MongoDB `UpdateFilter` object (e.g., `{ $set: { ... }, $unset: { ... } }`). The `hasChanges()` method allows checking if any modifications have been registered. The `getUpdateFilter()` method returns the final filter, but it also marks the updater as 'dirty' to prevent reuse and throws an error if no changes were registered, ensuring that update operations are only performed when meaningful modifications are present.

File Upload, UFS & Image Processing.text: Rocket.Chat employs the Unified File Store (UFS) system for comprehensive management of file uploads, storage, and processing. UFS provides an abstraction layer that allows for different storage back-ends, handles crucial aspects like upload validation, defines a clear lifecycle for files, and supports advanced features such as image processing and HTTP range requests for efficient content delivery. The core `UploadFS` object, defined in `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs.ts`, serves as the central hub for configuring and interacting with the file storage system.

The heart of the file management system is the `UploadFS` object, found in `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs.ts`. It acts as a singleton, providing access to configuration, registered storage back-ends, and utility functions. The `UploadFS.config` property, an instance of `Config` from `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-config.ts`, manages global settings such as `tmpDir` for temporary files, `storesPath`, and `https` options. Storage back-ends are registered and retrieved via `UploadFS.addStore(store: Store)` and `UploadFS.getStore(name: string)` respectively. The `Store` class (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-store.ts`) is an abstract base class that defines the common interface and lifecycle hooks for all storage implementations, ensuring consistency across different storage types. `UploadFS` also provides utilities like `generateEtag()` for unique identifiers and `getMimeType(extension: string)` for MIME type resolution.

UFS supports various storage back-ends by extending the abstract `Store` class (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-store.ts`). Rocket.Chat primarily uses two built-in implementations:

*   **LocalStore**: Defined in `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-local.ts`, this store saves files directly to the server's local file system. It uses Node.js `fs` module for operations like `fs.createReadStream`, `fs.createWriteStream`, and `fs.promises.unlink` for deletion. It handles directory creation (`mkdirp`) and permissions (`fs.chmod`) to ensure files are stored correctly. The `getPath` method constructs the full file path. `LocalStore` is registered as `UploadFS.store.Local`.

*   **GridFSStore**: Implemented in `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-gridfs.ts`, this store leverages MongoDB's GridFS for file storage. It utilizes `NpmModuleMongodb.GridFSBucket` to manage file chunks within the database. Key options include `chunkSize` and `collectionName`. `GridFSStore` is particularly notable for its handling of HTTP Range requests, adjusting the `end` option in `getReadStream` to ensure correct byte range delivery for media streaming. `GridFSStore` is registered as `UploadFS.store.GridFS`.

Both stores implement the `delete`, `getReadStream`, and `getWriteStream` methods, adapting them to their respective storage mechanisms.

File uploads undergo rigorous validation and filtering to ensure security and compliance with system policies. This is primarily handled by the `Filter` class, defined in `apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-filter.ts`. A `Filter` instance can be configured with various options:

*   `contentTypes`: An array of allowed MIME types (e.g., `['image/jpeg', 'image/*']`).
*   `extensions`: An array of allowed file extensions (e.g., `['jpg', 'png']`).
*   `minSize` and `maxSize`: Minimum and maximum allowed file sizes in bytes.
*   `onCheck`: A custom asynchronous function for additional validation logic.

The `Filter.check(file, content)` method performs these validations, throwing a `Meteor.Error` if any check fails (e.g., `file-too-large`, `invalid-file-extension`). The `Store` class (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-store.ts`) can be initialized with a `filter` option, and its `validate` method will invoke the filter's checks. For instance, the `ufsComplete` method (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-methods.ts`) explicitly calls `store.validate(file)` before finalizing an upload.

The `Store` class (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-store.ts`) defines a comprehensive set of lifecycle methods and hooks that allow for custom logic at various stages of an upload:

*   **`onValidate(file)`**: Called before a file is written to the store, allowing for final validation checks.
*   **`create(file)`**: Inserts file metadata into the associated MongoDB collection (`IUploadsModel`).
*   **`write(rs, fileId, callback)`**: The core method for writing a readable stream (`rs`) to the storage back-end. This is where `transformWrite` can be applied.
*   **`copy(fileId, store, callback)`**: Copies a file from the current store to another `Store` instance, involving `getReadStream` from the source and `write` to the destination.
*   **`transformRead(readStream, writeStream, fileId, file, request, headers)`**: Allows for transforming the file data as it is being read from the store.
*   **`transformWrite(readStream, writeStream, fileId, file)`**: Allows for transforming the file data as it is being written to the store.
*   **Error Hooks**: `onCopyError`, `onFinishUpload`, `onReadError`, `onWriteError` provide callbacks for handling errors during specific operations.

The `ufsComplete` Meteor method (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-methods.ts`) orchestrates the finalization of an upload. It reads the temporary file from `UploadFS.getTempFilePath(fileId)`, validates it using `store.validate(file)`, and then calls `store.write()` to move the file from temporary storage to its permanent location, finally removing the temporary file.

Image processing capabilities are integrated into the file upload workflow, primarily through the `UploadService` (`apps/meteor/server/services/upload/service.ts`). This service leverages the `sharp` library (imported in `service.ts`) for efficient image manipulation and metadata extraction. The `UploadService.extractMetadata(file: IUpload)` method is responsible for retrieving image dimensions (height, width) and format. When files are sent as messages, `UploadService.parseFileIntoMessageAttachments` processes the file, potentially generating thumbnails or extracting relevant image information to create appropriate message attachments. The `Uploads` model (`packages/models/src/models/Uploads.ts`) supports querying for images (`findImagesByRoomId`) and distinguishing between original files and their derivatives (e.g., thumbnails, identified by `typeGroup: 'thumb'`), which are managed by methods like `findAllByOriginalFileId` and `removeFileAndDerivates` during file deletion.

File Upload, UFS & Image Processing.section: HTTP Range Support and Content Delivery
File Upload, UFS & Image Processing.text:
Efficient content delivery, especially for large files or media streaming, relies on HTTP Range support. The UFS `Store` class (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-store.ts`) provides the `getReadStream(fileId, file, options?: { start?: number; end?: number })` method, which is designed to serve partial content.

*   **`LocalStore`** (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-local.ts`) implements `getReadStream` by passing the `start` and `end` options directly to `fs.createReadStream`, enabling native file system support for byte range requests.
*   **`GridFSStore`** (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-gridfs.ts`) implements `getReadStream` using `mongoStore.openDownloadStream`. Crucially, it adjusts the `end` option by incrementing it (`options.end += 1`) to correctly interpret 0-based inclusive ranges from HTTP `Content-Range` headers, preventing off-by-one errors that could lead to incomplete media playback. This ensures that browsers and media players can reliably request and receive specific portions of a file.

The `UploadFS.config.https` setting (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-config.ts`) also plays a role in securing content delivery over HTTPS.

Client-side upload coordination involves initiating the upload, potentially streaming file data, and then finalizing the process on the server. While the provided files focus on the server-side, the `ufsComplete` Meteor method (`apps/meteor/server/ufs/ufs-methods.ts`) is a key server endpoint that clients would invoke. After a file's raw data has been streamed to a temporary location (e.g., via a direct HTTP POST or DDP chunking, which is handled by other parts of the system not detailed here), the client calls `ufsComplete` with the `fileId` and `storeName`. This method then moves the temporary file to its permanent store. The `UploadService.uploadFile({ buffer, details })` method (`apps/meteor/server/services/upload/service.ts`) provides a higher-level API for clients or other server components to upload files by providing the complete file buffer and metadata, which then uses `FileUpload.getStore('Uploads').insert()` to persist the file. The `Uploads` MongoDB collection (`packages/models/src/models/Uploads.ts`) tracks the `complete` and `uploading` status of files, allowing the client to monitor the progress and final state of an upload.

Service Workers & Public Assets.text: Rocket.Chat leverages Service Workers to enhance client-side performance and enable advanced features like offline access and encrypted file handling. The client-side application, specifically `apps/meteor/client/serviceWorker.ts`, registers two primary Service Workers: one for static asset caching and another for decrypting files. The registration process checks for `serviceWorker` support in the `navigator` object and attempts to register `/enc.js` with a scope of `/`. If a Service Worker is active but not yet controlling the page, a `reload()` function is triggered to ensure activation, preventing issues with stale content by reloading the window after a short delay, managed by `localStorage` key `sw_last_reload`.

The static asset cache worker, defined in `apps/meteor/public/workers/index.js`, is responsible for caching and serving public assets to improve load times and provide basic offline capabilities. Upon `install`, it opens a cache named after its `version` ('MSW V0.3') and adds the root HTML path (`/`) to it, then `skipWaiting()` to activate immediately. During `activate`, it cleans up old caches by deleting any cache names that do not match the current `version`. The core logic resides in the `fetch` event listener. It attempts to `caches.match(event.request)` first. If a cached response exists, it checks if the resource is HTML or a hashed asset (CSS/JS). Non-HTML/non-hashed assets (like images) are returned directly from cache. For hashed assets, it verifies if the hash in the request URL matches the hash of the cached URL using `hasSameHash()`. If hashes match, the cached version is returned. Otherwise, or if no cache exists, it `fetch`es the resource from the network. Upon a successful network `response`, it clones the response and caches it. HTML responses are cached under the `HTMLToCache` key, while other assets are cached under their request URL. For hashed assets, it proactively deletes older versions of the same file (identified by `removeHash()`) before caching the new one. Requests to `/sockjs/` are explicitly excluded from caching and always fetched from the network, or a 'No connection' error is returned on failure.

The encrypted file download worker, located at `apps/meteor/public/enc.js`, is registered by `apps/meteor/client/serviceWorker.ts` to intercept and decrypt specific file download requests. It activates immediately on `install` and `claim()`s clients on `activate`. Its `fetch` event listener specifically targets URLs containing `/file-decrypt/`. For such requests, it extracts encryption parameters (`key`, `iv`, `name`, `type`) from the URL's query string using `getUrlParams()`. The `key` parameter is a base64-encoded JSON string containing the actual `key` and `iv` for decryption. After extracting parameters and rewriting the URL to remove the `/file-decrypt/` prefix and query parameters, it attempts to `caches.match()` the original request. If not found, it `fetch`es the raw encrypted file from the server. Once the file's `arrayBuffer` is obtained, the `decrypt()` function is called, utilizing `crypto.subtle.importKey()` with `jwk` format and `AES-CTR` algorithm, and `crypto.subtle.decrypt()` with the provided `key` and `iv` (decoded via `base64Decode()`). The decrypted `result` is then used to construct a new `Response` with appropriate `Content-Disposition` and `Content-Type` headers, making the file available to the browser. This decrypted response is also cached for future access. Additionally, this worker handles `message` events of type `attachment-download`, allowing the client application to request decryption of a file directly via a message, receiving the `result` back through `event.source.postMessage()`.

The End-to-End Encryption (E2EE) key lifecycle is managed by several modules, with `apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/keychain.ts` acting as the central manager for user private keys. The `Keychain` class handles the encryption and decryption of a user's private key using a password. Stored keys can be in `IStoredKeyV1` (binary with IV prefix) or `IStoredKeyV2` (JSON with separate `iv`, `ciphertext`, `salt`, `iterations`) formats. The `decryptKey()` method takes an encrypted private key string and a password. It decodes the stored key using `EncryptedKeyCodec`, determines the AES algorithm (`AES-CBC` for v1, `AES-GCM` for v2), then uses `Pbkdf2.importBaseKey()` to create a base key from the password. `Pbkdf2.derive()` generates `DerivedBits` (a 32-byte key) using the provided `salt` and `iterations` (from the stored key options). Finally, `Pbkdf2.importKey()` creates an `AES` key from these derived bits, which is then used by `Pbkdf2.decrypt()` to decrypt the private key content. The `encryptKey()` method reverses this process, generating a new `salt` and `iterations` (100,000 for `AES-GCM`), deriving a key, and encrypting the private key content. The `apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/crypto/aes.ts` module provides symmetric AES-GCM/CBC operations (`generate`, `importKey`, `exportJwk`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`) for general data and group session keys. The `apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/crypto/rsa.ts` module handles asymmetric RSA-OAEP key pairs (`generate`, `exportPublicKey`, `exportPrivateKey`, `importPrivateKey`, `importPublicKey`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`), typically used for secure key exchange. The `E2ERoom` class in `apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/rocketchat.e2e.room.ts` orchestrates the E2EE state for a specific room, managing the `groupSessionKey` (an `Aes.Key`) and `oldKeys`, and handling the decryption of messages and subscriptions once the room is `READY`.

License and statistics tokens within Rocket.Chat are cryptographically secured using the module `ee/packages/license/src/token.ts`. This module provides functions to `decrypt()` and `decryptStatsToken()` these tokens. For license tokens, it distinguishes between V2 and V3 formats. V2 licenses are decrypted using `crypto.publicDecrypt()` with a hardcoded `PUBLIC_LICENSE_KEY_V2` (an RSA public key). V3 licenses are identified by the `RCV3_` prefix and are verified using the `@rocket.chat/jwt` library's `verify()` function against the `PUBLIC_LICENSE_KEY_V3` (which is a base64-decoded version of `PUBLIC_LICENSE_KEY_V2`). Similarly, statistics tokens are verified using `verify()` against `PUBLIC_STATS_KEY_V2`. In a `test` environment, the module can generate and use temporary key pairs via `getPairs()` for `encrypt()` and `encryptStatsToken()` functions, allowing for testing of the signing and verification process without relying on production keys.

The Rocket.Chat client initiates its lifecycle by registering two Service Workers: one for static assets (`apps/meteor/public/workers/index.js`) and another for encrypted files (`apps/meteor/public/enc.js`). The static worker intercepts all network requests, serving cached assets where possible, and fetching/caching new or updated content from the Rocket.Chat server. The encrypted file worker specifically intercepts `/file-decrypt/` URLs, extracts encryption parameters, fetches the raw encrypted file from the server, and then uses the `AES-CTR` algorithm (via `crypto.subtle`) to decrypt the content before returning it to the client and caching the decrypted result. For End-to-End Encryption, the `E2EE Keychain Manager` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/keychain.ts`) handles the secure storage and retrieval of a user's private key. This involves deriving a symmetric key from the user's password and a salt using `PBKDF2` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/crypto/pbkdf2.ts`), which is then used with `AES` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/crypto/aes.ts`) to encrypt or decrypt the private key. Room-specific E2EE is managed by `E2E Room Manager` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/rocketchat.e2e.room.ts`), which utilizes `AES` for group session keys and `RSA` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/crypto/rsa.ts`) for key exchange. Finally, license and statistics tokens are processed by `License Token Cryptography` (`ee/packages/license/src/token.ts`), which verifies their authenticity using RSA public-key cryptography or JWT verification against embedded public keys.

OAuth2 Server, Personal Access Tokens &.section: OAuth2 Server, Personal Access Tokens & Session
OAuth2 Server, Personal Access Tokens &.text: Rocket.Chat implements an OAuth2 server for third-party application integration and provides Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for programmatic access. These mechanisms allow external services and scripts to authenticate and interact with the Rocket.Chat API, managing user sessions and permissions. The core OAuth2 functionality is handled by an `OAuth2Server` class, which uses a `Model` to interact with various MongoDB collections for tokens and applications. PATs are managed directly within the `Users` collection, primarily for authenticating users during the OAuth2 authorization flow, rather than directly for API v1 requests.

The OAuth2 server's data interactions are abstracted by the `Model` class located in `apps/meteor/server/oauth2-server/model.ts`. This class implements `AuthorizationCodeModel` and `RefreshTokenModel` from `@node-oauth/oauth2-server`, defining how the OAuth2 server interacts with Rocket.Chat's database. Key methods include:
  • `getAccessToken(accessToken: string)`: Retrieves an access token and its associated client and user from `OAuthAccessTokens`.
  • `getClient(clientId: string, clientSecret?: string)`: Fetches an active OAuth application from `OAuthApps` using `findOneActiveByClientId` or `findOneActiveByClientIdAndClientSecret`.
  • `getAuthorizationCode(authorizationCode: string)`: Retrieves an authorization code from `OAuthAuthCodes`.
  • `saveAuthorizationCode(...)`: Stores an authorization code in `OAuthAuthCodes`.
  • `saveToken(...)`: Persists access and refresh tokens in `OAuthAccessTokens`.
The `Model` class maintains a list of supported `grants` (currently `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`).

OAuth applications are registered and managed within Rocket.Chat. The `OAuthApps` collection (`packages/models/src/models/OAuthApps.ts`) stores details about each registered application, including `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `redirectUri`, and `active` status. New OAuth applications can be added via the `addOAuthApp` function (`apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/admin/functions/addOAuthApp.ts`). This function validates input parameters like `name` and `redirectUri`, generates unique `clientId` and `clientSecret` using `Random.id()` and `Random.secret()`, and then inserts the application into the `OAuthApps` collection. It also requires the user performing the action to have the `manage-oauth-apps` permission. The `redirectUri` can be a comma or newline-separated list, parsed by `parseUriList` (`apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/admin/functions/parseUriList.ts`).

Personal Access Tokens (PATs) provide a way for users to generate API tokens for programmatic access without exposing their main credentials. PATs are stored directly within the `services.resume.loginTokens` array of the `Users` collection (`packages/models/src/models/Users.ts`).
  • **Generation**: The `personalAccessTokens:generateToken` Meteor method (`apps/meteor/imports/personal-access-tokens/server/api/methods/generateToken.ts`) handles PAT creation. It requires the `create-personal-access-tokens` permission. A unique token is generated using `Random.secret()`, hashed with `Accounts._hashLoginToken()`, and then added to the user's `loginTokens` array in the `Users` collection via `Users.addPersonalAccessTokenToUser`.
  • **Regeneration**: The `personalAccessTokens:regenerateToken` method (`apps/meteor/imports/personal-access-tokens/server/api/methods/regenerateToken.ts`) first removes an existing token by name using `removePersonalAccessTokenOfUser` and then calls `generatePersonalAccessTokenOfUser` to create a new one, preserving the `bypassTwoFactor` setting.
Both generation and regeneration methods are protected by `twoFactorRequired`. While PATs are login tokens, based on the provided files, they are primarily used to authenticate the user during the OAuth2 authorization grant process, not directly for `API.v1` requests.

Rocket.Chat's API routing integrates the OAuth2 server for authentication. The `OAuth2Server` instance (`oauth2server` in `apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/oauth/oauth2-server.ts`) is an Express application mounted under `/oauth/*` using `WebApp.connectHandlers`. It defines routes for:
  • `/oauth/token`: Handles token requests (e.g., exchanging authorization codes for access tokens). It uses `oauth.token()` from `@node-oauth/oauth2-server`.
  • `/oauth/authorize`: Manages authorization requests. The `GET` route verifies client IDs and redirect URIs. The `POST` route authenticates the user, potentially using a login token (which could be a Personal Access Token) via `Users.findOne({'services.resume.loginTokens.hashedToken': Accounts._hashLoginToken(req.body.access_token)})`, and then updates the `oauth.authorizedClients` array in the `Users` collection before issuing an authorization code.
  • `/oauth/userinfo`: Provides user information based on an access token, querying `OAuthAccessTokens` and `Users`.
For general API v1 requests, an authentication method is added to `API.v1` (`apps/meteor/app/api/server/ApiClass.ts`) using `API.v1.addAuthMethod`. This method calls `oAuth2ServerAuth` (`apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/oauth/oauth2-server.ts`), which extracts the bearer token or `access_token` from the request, retrieves the corresponding access token from `OAuthAccessTokens` using `OAuthAccessTokens.findOneByAccessToken`, and then fetches the `User` from the `Users` collection using `Users.findOneById`. This mechanism *only* authenticates using OAuth2 access tokens for `API.v1` endpoints.

1. **OAuth App Registration**: An admin uses `addOAuthApp` (`apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/admin/functions/addOAuthApp.ts`) to register an application, which generates `clientId`/`clientSecret` and stores them in `OAuthApps` (`packages/models/src/models/OAuthApps.ts`).2. **Personal Access Token (PAT) Management**: A user generates a PAT via `personalAccessTokens:generateToken` (`apps/meteor/imports/personal-access-tokens/server/api/methods/generateToken.ts`). A hashed token is stored in the user's `services.resume.loginTokens` array within the `Users` collection (`packages/models/src/models/Users.ts`).3. **OAuth Authorization Flow**:
  • A client redirects a user to `/oauth/authorize`.
  • The `OAuth2Server` (`apps/meteor/server/oauth2-server/oauth.ts`) validates the client and prompts the user for consent.
  • During the `POST /oauth/authorize` step, the user's session is authenticated. This authentication can happen via a login token (e.g., a PAT) by checking `Users.findOne({'services.resume.loginTokens.hashedToken': ...})`.
  • Upon user approval, an authorization code is saved in `OAuthAuthCodes` via `Model.saveAuthorizationCode` (`apps/meteor/server/oauth2-server/model.ts`).
  • The client exchanges the authorization code at `/oauth/token`.
  • The `OAuth2Server` (via `Model.getAuthorizationCode` and `Model.saveToken`) validates the code and issues an access token and optionally a refresh token, storing them in `OAuthAccessTokens`.
4. **OAuth API Access**:
  • A client sends an API request to `API.v1` with an OAuth access token.
  • `API.v1.addAuthMethod` (`apps/meteor/app/api/server/ApiClass.ts`) calls `oAuth2ServerAuth` (`apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/oauth/oauth2-server.ts`), which retrieves the token from `OAuthAccessTokens` and the user from `Users`.
  • **Note**: Based on the provided files, Personal Access Tokens are *not* directly used to authenticate `API.v1` requests; they are primarily for authenticating the user during the OAuth2 authorization grant process.

Engagement, NPS Surveys & Version Checks.text: The Rocket.Chat platform incorporates features for user engagement through Net Promoter Score (NPS) surveys and system maintenance via version checks. NPS surveys gather valuable user feedback, while the version check system ensures the server is running the latest software, informing administrators about available updates and critical alerts. Both systems rely on scheduled tasks, database interactions, and communication with external services to function, providing a proactive approach to user satisfaction and system health.

The NPS survey pipeline is managed primarily by the `NPSService` (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/service.ts`).

**Survey Creation:** A new NPS survey can be initiated by calling `NPSService.create`. This method first verifies that the `NPS_survey_enabled` setting is active. If enabled, it saves the survey details (ID, start/expire dates, creator, status `NPSStatus.OPEN`) to the `Nps` collection (`packages/models/src/models/Nps.ts`). Concurrently, it creates an administrative banner using `getBannerForAdmins` and sends notifications to administrators via `notifyAdmins` (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/notification.ts`), informing them about the upcoming survey.

Separately, the `getAndCreateNpsSurvey` function (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/getAndCreateNpsSurvey.ts`) can fetch survey data from an external `Nps_Url` (configured via settings) using `serverFetch` and `getWorkspaceAccessToken`. This external data is then used to create a `Banner` within Rocket.Chat, making the survey visible to users.

**User Voting:** When a user submits an NPS vote, the `NPSService.vote` method is invoked. It validates the `npsId` and ensures the survey is `NPSStatus.OPEN` and within its active period. A unique `identifier` for the vote is generated by hashing the `userId` and `npsId` using `createHash('sha256')`. The vote details (timestamp, `npsId`, identifier, roles, score, comment, and `INpsVoteStatus.NEW` status) are then saved to the `NpsVote` collection (`packages/models/src/models/NpsVote.ts`).

**Sending Results:** The process of sending NPS results is handled by `NPSService.sendResults`, which is typically triggered by a daily cron job (`npsCron` in `apps/meteor/server/cron/nps.ts`) at 15:21 UTC. This function performs the following steps:
1. It checks if NPS is enabled and retrieves any `NPSStatus.OPEN` or `NPSStatus.SENDING` surveys that have expired (`Nps.getOpenExpiredAndStartSending`, `Nps.getOpenExpiredAlreadySending`).
2. It fetches unsent votes (status `INpsVoteStatus.NEW`) from the `NpsVote` collection using `NpsVote.findNotSentByNpsId`.
3. For each batch of votes, it updates their status to `INpsVoteStatus.SENDING`.
4. The votes are then sent to the external NPS service via `sendNpsResults` (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/sendNpsResults.ts`), which uses `serverFetch` and `getWorkspaceAccessToken` to POST the data to `${Nps_Url}/v1/surveys/${npsId}/results`.
5. Upon successful transmission, the votes' status in the `NpsVote` collection is updated to `INpsVoteStatus.SENT` using `NpsVote.updateVotesToSent`.
6. If there are still votes remaining to be sent for a survey, `NPSService.sendResults` schedules itself to run again after 5 minutes using `setTimeout`.
7. To prevent votes from getting stuck, `NpsVote.updateOldSendingToNewByNpsId` reverts any votes in `INpsVoteStatus.SENDING` status for more than 5 minutes back to `INpsVoteStatus.NEW`.
8. Once all votes for a survey have been sent, the survey's status in the `Nps` collection is updated to `NPSStatus.SENT` using `Nps.updateStatusById`. The `npsCron` also calls `NPS.closeOpenSurveys` if NPS is disabled, setting all `NPSStatus.OPEN` surveys to `NPSStatus.CLOSED`.

The Rocket.Chat version check system ensures administrators are informed about new software updates and critical alerts. The core logic resides in the `version-check` module (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/`).

**Triggering Checks:** The `checkVersionUpdate` function (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/functions/checkVersionUpdate.ts`) is the entry point. It's executed on `Meteor.startup` if the `Update_EnableChecker` setting is true, and subsequently by a daily cron job named `version_check` (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/index.ts`) scheduled for 02:00 UTC. The cron job's existence is dynamically managed: it's added or removed based on changes to the `Update_EnableChecker` setting.

**Fetching Updates:** Inside `checkVersionUpdate`, the `getNewUpdates` function (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/functions/getNewUpdates.ts`) is called. This function gathers various server details, including the `uniqueID` (from `Settings` collection), current `Info.version`, OS information (`os.type`, `os.platform`, `os.arch`, `os.release`), and Node.js version (`process.version`). It then uses `getWorkspaceAccessToken` to authenticate and `serverFetch` to query the Rocket.Chat release service at `https://releases.rocket.chat/updates/check`. The response is expected to contain a list of `versions` (available updates) and `alerts` (important messages).

**Processing Versions:** The `buildVersionUpdateMessage` function (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/functions/buildVersionUpdateMessage.ts`) processes the `versions` data. It first calls `cleanupOutdatedVersionUpdateBanners` to remove any `versionUpdate-*` banners from admin users that are no longer relevant (e.g., for versions older than the current one). It then compares the fetched versions with the `Update_LatestAvailableVersion` setting and the server's `Info.version` using `semver`. If a newer stable version is identified, the `Update_LatestAvailableVersion` setting is updated via `updateAuditedBySystem` and `Settings.updateValueById`, and administrators are notified with messages and banners using `sendMessagesToAdmins`.

**Processing Alerts:** The `showAlertsFromCloud` function (also called by `checkVersionUpdate`) handles the `alerts` received from the release service. It checks `Users.bannerExistsById` to ensure that administrators are not repeatedly notified about alerts they have already dismissed. For new or undismissed alerts, it constructs and sends messages and banners to administrators using `sendMessagesToAdmins`, with banner IDs formatted as `alert-{alert.id}`.

The engagement and version check systems involve several key components and data flows:

**NPS Survey Flow:**
- An administrator or system event triggers `NPSService.create` (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/service.ts`), which writes survey data to the `Nps` collection (`nps_db`) and sends notifications/banners to `admin_notifications`.
- The `get_create_nps_survey_func` (`apps/meteor/server/services/nps/getAndCreateNpsSurvey.ts`) fetches survey definitions from the `external_nps_api` and creates banners for `admin_notifications`.
- `user_client` interactions (votes) are sent to `nps_service`, which then writes them to the `NpsVote` collection (`nps_db`).
- The `nps_cron` (`apps/meteor/server/cron/nps.ts`) periodically invokes `nps_service`'s `sendResults` method.
- `nps_service` reads votes from `nps_db`, uses `cloud_workspace_token` for authentication, and sends aggregated results to the `external_nps_api`.
- `nps_service` updates the status of surveys and votes in `nps_db`.

**Version Check Flow:**
- The `version_check_cron` (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/index.ts`) or `rc_server` startup triggers the `version_check_module` (`apps/meteor/app/version-check/server/functions/*`).
- `version_check_module` reads settings (e.g., `uniqueID`, `Update_EnableChecker`) from `settings_collection`.
- It uses `cloud_workspace_token` to authenticate requests to the `release_service` (`https://releases.rocket.chat`).
- `release_service` responds with available `versions` and `alerts`.
- `version_check_module` processes this data, updating `Update_LatestAvailableVersion` in `settings_collection`.
- It also manages `versionUpdate-*` and `alert-*` banners in `users_collection` (specifically for admin users) and sends messages/banners to `admin_notifications`.

Emoji, Custom Sounds & Custom Status.text: Rocket.Chat provides robust support for emojis, custom sounds, and custom user statuses, enhancing user expression and communication. This system integrates standard emoji packages like EmojiOne, allows for the creation and management of custom emojis, and provides mechanisms for custom sounds and user statuses, although specific implementation details for the latter two are not covered in the provided files.

The core emoji system is defined by the `EmojiPackages` and `EmojiPackage` types in `apps/meteor/app/emoji/lib/rocketchat.ts`. The `EmojiPackages` type holds a collection of `packages` (e.g., 'base', 'emojiCustom') and a comprehensive `list` mapping emoji shortnames to their data. Each `EmojiPackage` defines `emojiCategories`, `emojisByCategory`, `toneList`, and crucial `render` and `renderPicker` functions. The client-side `emoji` object, found in `apps/meteor/app/emoji/client/lib.ts`, extends `EmojiPackages` with a `dispatchUpdate` method, which uses `emojiEmitter` to signal changes. The server-side `emoji` object in `apps/meteor/app/emoji/server/lib.ts` provides a base structure, primarily for `renderPicker` logic that delegates to the correct package's renderer. The `base` package on the client uses `emojione.toImage` for its `render` function, while the server's `base` package simply returns the message as-is.

Emoji parsing and rendering on the client-side is primarily handled by the `emojiParser` function in `apps/meteor/app/emoji/client/emojiParser.ts`. This function takes an HTML string and performs several transformations: it normalizes apostrophes (`'` to `'`) and line breaks (`
` to `
`), then iterates through all registered `emoji.packages` in reverse order, applying each package's `render` function to convert shortcodes or Unicode characters into visual emoji representations. After rendering, it inspects the resulting HTML for `.emoji` or `.emojione` elements. Emojis found within `` tags are reverted to their text form. It also determines if a message consists solely of emojis to apply a 'big' class for larger display. Finally, it reverts the apostrophe and line break normalizations. For React component rendering, the `Emoji` component in `packages/gazzodown/src/emoji/Emoji.tsx` is responsible for displaying emoji nodes from the message parser output, conditionally rendering `EmojiRenderer` or `PlainSpan` based on `useEmoji` and `convertAsciiToEmoji` context values.

The `emojione` library, used for standard emoji rendering, is configured and extended in `apps/meteor/app/emoji-emojione/lib/getEmojiConfig.ts`. This file addresses several known issues with the upstream `emojione` library. It manually adds missing emojis (like `:tm:`, `:copyright:`, and various digit symbols) to `emojione.shortnames` and `emojione.emojioneList` to ensure they are correctly recognized and rendered. Furthermore, it includes a specific fix for the `:+1:` emoji by modifying the `convertShortName` function to properly escape the `+` character in regular expressions. To optimize performance, `emojione.shortnameConversionMap` and `emojione.unicodeCharRegex` are memoized using the `mem` utility, caching their results for a short period.

The lifecycle of custom emojis involves both server-side management and client-side rendering. On the server, the `insertOrUpdateEmoji` method in `apps/meteor/app/emoji-custom/server/methods/insertOrUpdateEmoji.ts` is the entry point for creating or updating custom emojis. This method delegates to `uploadEmojiCustomWithBuffer` in `apps/meteor/app/emoji-custom/server/lib/uploadEmojiCustom.ts`. This function requires the `manage-emoji` permission, sanitizes the emoji name using `limax`, processes the image file (e.g., converting SVG to PNG with `sharp`, resizing with `Media.resizeFromBuffer`), stores it via `RocketChatFileEmojiCustomInstance`, and updates the `EmojiCustom` MongoDB collection (`packages/models/src/models/EmojiCustom.ts`) with an `etag`. After successful upload, it broadcasts an `emoji.updateCustom` event to all clients. On the client, `apps/meteor/client/lib/customEmoji.ts` handles these updates. The `updateEmojiCustom` function modifies the client-side `emoji.list` and `emoji.packages.emojiCustom.emojisByCategory.rocket` to reflect changes, including aliases, and calls `emoji.dispatchUpdate()` to notify components like the emoji picker. Similarly, `deleteEmojiCustom` removes the emoji from these client-side registries. The `customRender` function in this file dynamically generates a regular expression (`emoji.packages.emojiCustom._regexp`) to match custom emoji shortnames and replaces them with `<span>` elements pointing to the custom emoji's URL via `getEmojiUrlFromName`.
