Outlook Calendar Integration & Status Sy.text: This page details the integration of Outlook Calendar events within Rocket.Chat, focusing on how events are displayed, how users can join calls, and how their Rocket.Chat status is automatically synchronized with their calendar availability. The integration involves both client-side components for user interaction and server-side logic for managing events and status updates.

The Outlook Calendar integration primarily functions through the Rocket.Chat Desktop application for authentication and credential management. On the client, React hooks and components handle displaying calendar events and facilitating joining calls. Server-side, a dedicated `CalendarService` (`apps/meteor/server/services/calendar/service.ts`) manages the persistence of calendar events, schedules notifications, and orchestrates user status synchronization based on event busy/free status. This synchronization is achieved via cron jobs that trigger status changes and broadcast updates across the system.

Client-side features requiring interaction with the desktop application, such as Outlook authentication, are protected by an error boundary mechanism. Specifically, the `NotOnDesktopError` class (`apps/meteor/client/views/outlookCalendar/lib/NotOnDesktopError.ts`) is thrown when an attempt is made to access desktop-specific functionalities (e.g., `window.RocketChatDesktop.hasOutlookCredentials`) outside of the desktop environment. This custom error extends `RocketChatError` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/errors/RocketChatError.ts`), providing a structured way to handle application-specific errors with an `error` ID and optional `reason` and `details`.

Authentication with Outlook Calendar is managed through a set of React hooks in `apps/meteor/client/views/outlookCalendar/hooks/useOutlookAuthentication.ts`. The `useOutlookAuthentication` hook queries the desktop app via `window.RocketChatDesktop.hasOutlookCredentials()` to determine if Outlook credentials are set. If not on desktop or credentials are missing, it throws a `NotOnDesktopError`. `useOutlookAuthenticationMutationLogout` handles the logout process. It calls `window.RocketChatDesktop.clearOutlookCredentials()` to remove stored credentials in the desktop app, then invalidates relevant queries to update the UI, and dispatches a success toast message. These mutations ensure that authentication state is correctly reflected and managed.

When a user interacts with an Outlook calendar event, the `OutlookCalendarEventModal` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/outlookCalendar/OutlookCalendarEventModal.tsx`) is displayed. This modal fetches detailed event information. If an `id` is provided, it queries the server's `/v1/calendar-events.info` endpoint. Otherwise, it uses locally provided `subject`, `meetingUrl`, and `description`. The modal utilizes the `useOutlookOpenCall` hook to provide a "Join call" button, which, when clicked, initiates the meeting. A `GenericModalSkeleton` is shown during loading.

Individual Outlook calendar events are rendered by the `OutlookEventItem` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/outlookCalendar/OutlookEventsList/OutlookEventItem.tsx`). Each item displays the event `subject` and `startTime`. Clicking an event item triggers `handleOpenEvent`, which uses `useSetModal` to open the `OutlookCalendarEventModal` for detailed viewing. If a `meetingUrl` is present, a "Join" button is displayed. This button's `onClick` handler, `handleMeetingClick`, uses `usePreventPropagation` to prevent the event from bubbling up and then calls `openCall`. The `useOutlookOpenCall` hook (`apps/meteor/client/views/outlookCalendar/hooks/useOutlookOpenCall.ts`) is central to joining calls. It takes a `meetingUrl`, appends the user's display name (`&name=${userDisplayName}`), and then delegates to `useVideoConfOpenCall` (`apps/meteor/client/views/room/contextualBar/VideoConference/hooks/useVideoConfOpenCall`) to open the video conference link.

The core server-side logic resides in the `CalendarService` (`apps/meteor/server/services/calendar/service.ts`). This service is responsible for: Event Management: Methods like `create`, `import`, `get`, `list`, `update`, and `delete` interact with the `CalendarEvent` MongoDB collection (`packages/models/src/models/CalendarEvent.ts`) to store and retrieve calendar events. The `CalendarEventRaw` model provides methods like `findByUserIdAndDate`, `updateEvent`, and `findOneByExternalIdAndUserId`. Status Scheduling: When events are created or updated, `CalendarService` calls `this.setupNextStatusChange()` to schedule cron jobs. These jobs are uniquely identified using `generateCronJobId` (`apps/meteor/server/services/calendar/statusEvents/generateCronJobId.ts`). Status Application: Scheduled cron jobs execute the `applyStatusChange` logic (revealed in `apps/meteor/tests/unit/server/services/calendar/statusEvents/applyStatusChange.ts`). This function fetches the user from `Users` model, determines the new status (defaulting to `UserStatus.BUSY` if not specified), updates the user's status via `Users.updateStatusAndStatusDefault`, and broadcasts the `presence.status` update using `api.broadcast`. This ensures real-time status reflection across the Rocket.Chat client. Cron Job Management: The service also handles `removeCronJobs` and `cancelUpcomingStatusChanges` to manage the lifecycle of scheduled status updates. The `CalendarEventRaw` model includes methods like `findOverlappingEvents` and `findEventsToScheduleNow` to assist in scheduling and managing status changes.

The Outlook Calendar integration follows a clear data flow. On the client, the Rocket.Chat UI (`rc_client_ui`) interacts with `outlook_auth_hooks` to authenticate via the `rc_desktop_app`. Calendar events are displayed through `outlook_event_item` and `outlook_event_modal`, which can fetch details from `rc_server_endpoints` (calling `calendar_service`). Both event components can trigger `video_conf_hook` to open `external_meeting` URLs. Server-side, `calendar_service` persists events in `calendar_event_model` and schedules `cron_scheduler` tasks. These tasks, handled by `status_change_handler`, update user statuses in `users_model` and notify clients via `rc_api_broadcast`, which in turn updates the `rc_client_ui`.

Invite Links, Conference Pages & Error P.section: Invite Links, Conference Pages & Error Pages
Invite Links, Conference Pages & Error P.text: This section introduces how Rocket.Chat handles various user entry points and states, including invite links for SAML authentication, dedicated landing pages for video conferences, and user-friendly error displays. It covers the flow from initial URL parsing to rendering the appropriate UI or initiating actions.

The invite link flow, specifically for SAML, is managed by the `useSamlInviteToken` hook in `apps/meteor/client/views/invite/hooks/useSamlInviteToken.ts`. This hook utilizes `useRouteParameter('hash')` to extract a `hash` parameter from the URL, which is expected to be the SAML invite token. The token is then stored in session storage using `useSessionStorage` with the key `saml_invite_token`. If no `hash` parameter is present, `null` is stored. This mechanism ensures that the SAML invite token persists across redirects or page reloads within the session, allowing the SAML authentication process to pick it up later.

The video conference landing page is primarily handled by `ConferenceRoute` and `ConferencePage`.
The `ConferenceRoute` component in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferenceRoute.tsx` acts as an entry point, wrapping the `ConferencePage` with an `AuthenticationCheck` component. This ensures that the user is authenticated (or a guest, as specified by the `guest` prop) before accessing the conference page.

The `ConferencePage` component in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferencePage.tsx` is responsible for processing the video conference URL and initiating the call. It first extracts the `callUrl` parameter from the browser's query string using `getQueryParams`. If a `callUrl` is present, it retrieves the current user's display name via `useUserDisplayName` and appends it to the `callUrl` as a `name` parameter.
An `useEffect` hook then triggers the `handleOpenCall` function (obtained from `useVideoConfOpenCall`) with the prepared `callUrl`. After initiating the call, the user is redirected to the `home` route using `defaultRoute.push()`.
If no `callUrl` is found in the URL parameters, `ConferencePage` renders the `ConferencePageError` component.

Error handling for the video conference landing page is managed by `ConferencePageError` in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferencePageError.tsx`. This component is rendered by `ConferencePage` when the `callUrl` query parameter is missing.
`ConferencePageError` displays a user-friendly error message, "Call not found", along with a subtitle explaining the issue. It uses `States`, `StatesIcon`, `StatesTitle`, and `StatesSubtitle` from `@rocket.chat/fuselage` for consistent UI.
If the user is not logged in (checked via `useUser`), an action button "Back to login" is displayed. Clicking this button redirects the user to the `login` route using `route.push()`.

Several cross-cutting concerns are evident in these components. Authentication is a key aspect, handled by `AuthenticationCheck` in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferenceRoute.tsx`, which ensures that access to sensitive pages like `ConferencePage` is restricted or managed appropriately for guests.
Session management is utilized by `useSamlInviteToken` in `apps/meteor/client/views/invite/hooks/useSamlInviteToken.ts` to persist the SAML invite token across browser sessions using `useSessionStorage`.
Routing and navigation are managed through `useRoute` and `useRouteParameter` from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts`, allowing components to read URL parameters and programmatically navigate to different routes (e.g., `home`, `login`).
Internationalization is supported via `useTranslation` in `apps/meteor/client/views/conference/ConferencePageError.tsx`, ensuring error messages are localized.
Finally, the `useUser` and `useUserDisplayName` hooks provide consistent access to user information across different parts of the application.

Home Page, Banners & Announcements.text: The Rocket.Chat home page serves as a central hub, providing users with quick access to features and information. Its content is highly customizable, allowing administrators to tailor the user experience. Key elements include a customizable header and various content cards, including a dedicated custom content block. Alongside the static and configurable home page content, the system also features a dynamic banner and announcement system. This system displays important messages to users, which can be either legacy-style banners or more interactive UiKit-based banners, and includes specific mechanisms for user-targeted announcements.

The home page's structure is composed of several React components. The header is managed by `apps/meteor/client/views/home/HomePageHeader.tsx`, which displays a title derived from the `Layout_Home_Title` setting (accessed via `useSetting`). If the user has `EDIT_LAYOUT_PERMISSIONS`, a 'Customize' button is shown, navigating to the `admin-settings` route for the 'Layout' group.

Central to the home page's flexibility is the `CustomContentCard` component in `apps/meteor/client/views/home/cards/CustomContentCard.tsx`. This card renders content from the `Layout_Home_Body` setting using the `CustomHomepageContent` component. Administrators (checked via `useRole('admin')`) have controls to manage the visibility of this custom content (`Layout_Home_Custom_Block_Visible`) and to make it the *only* content displayed on the home page (`Layout_Custom_Body_Only`). These settings are updated using `useSettingSetValue`.

Other functional cards, such as `CreateChannelsCard` (`apps/meteor/client/views/home/cards/CreateChannelsCard.tsx`), `MobileAppsCard` (`apps/meteor/client/views/home/cards/MobileAppsCard.tsx`), and `DocumentationCard` (`apps/meteor/client/views/home/cards/DocumentationCard.tsx`), provide quick actions or links. These cards leverage the `GenericCard` component for consistent styling and functionality.

The banner system is orchestrated by the `banners` utility in `apps/meteor/client/lib/banners.ts`. This utility maintains a `queue` of `BannerPayload` objects and uses an `Emitter` to notify subscribers of updates. Banners can be added to the queue using `banners.open` and removed using `banners.closeById` or `banners.close`.

The `BannerPayload` can be either a `LegacyBannerPayload` (a simpler, older format) or a `UiKit.BannerView` (for more interactive, app-driven banners). The `isLegacyPayload` function distinguishes between these types.

`BannerRegion` (`apps/meteor/client/views/banners/BannerRegion.tsx`) is the primary component responsible for rendering banners. It uses `useSyncExternalStore` to subscribe to `banners.firstSubscription`, which provides the topmost banner from the queue. Depending on the payload type, `BannerRegion` conditionally renders either a `LegacyBanner` (`apps/meteor/client/views/banners/LegacyBanner.tsx`) or a `UiKitBanner` (`apps/meteor/client/views/banners/UiKitBanner.tsx`).

`LegacyBanner` handles basic display, optional timers, actions, and close callbacks. `UiKitBanner` integrates with the UiKit rendering system, using `UiKitContext.Provider`, `UiKitComponent`, `useUiKitView`, and `useUiKitActionManager` to process and render complex UiKit views. When a UiKit banner is closed, it emits a `viewClosed` interaction via the `actionManager`.

The data flow for the home page and banners involves client-side settings, server-side data, and reactive updates.

**Home Page Customization Flow:**
1. An administrator navigates to the 'Layout' settings via the `admin-settings` route (triggered by `HomePageHeader.tsx` or `CustomContentCard.tsx`).
2. They modify settings like `Layout_Home_Title`, `Layout_Home_Body`, `Layout_Home_Custom_Block_Visible`, or `Layout_Custom_Body_Only`.
3. These settings are persisted and then retrieved on the client-side by components like `HomePageHeader.tsx` and `CustomContentCard.tsx` using the `useSetting` hook.
4. `CustomContentCard.tsx` then renders the `CustomHomepageContent` based on these settings, controlling its visibility and whether it's the sole content.

**Banner & Announcement Flow:**
1. **Server-side Banners:** Banners are managed in the database by `BannersRaw` (`packages/models/src/models/Banners.ts`). This model provides methods like `create`, `createOrUpdate`, and `findActiveByRoleOrId` to manage banner lifecycle and targeting.
2. **User-specific Banners:** The `useUserBanners` hook (`apps/meteor/client/views/banners/hooks/useUserBanners.ts`) observes the `user.banners` property (part of the client's `useUser` data). This property is populated by the server with active banners relevant to the current user.
3. When `user.banners` updates and an unread banner is found, `useUserBanners` calls `banners.open` to add it to the client-side banner queue in `apps/meteor/client/lib/banners.ts`.
4. `BannerRegion.tsx` subscribes to this queue via `banners.firstSubscription` and renders the top banner, either as a `LegacyBanner` or `UiKitBanner`.
5. **Dismissal:** If a user closes a legacy banner that originated from `user.banners`, the `onClose` callback in `LegacyBanner.tsx` triggers `dismissUserBanner` via `useDismissUserBannerMutation.ts`. This mutation calls the `banner/dismiss` method on the server, which updates the banner's status in the database via `BannersRaw`, eventually reflecting in `user.banners` and removing the banner from the client.

Account Profile & Client Startup.text: The client-side management of a user's account profile and its initialization during startup involves several interconnected components, from data retrieval and form handling to UI rendering and reactive updates. This process ensures that user-specific settings and profile details are consistently displayed and modifiable, while also integrating with broader client-side reactivity and accessibility features. Key aspects include the initial population of profile forms, dynamic application of user preferences like font styles, registration of account-related navigation items, and reactive observation of user data changes.

The `AccountProfilePage` component, located at `apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/AccountProfilePage.tsx`, serves as the primary entry point for managing a user's profile. It leverages `react-hook-form` for efficient form state management. Upon initialization, `AccountProfilePage` calls `getProfileInitialValues(user)` from `apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/getProfileInitialValues.ts` to populate the form's `defaultValues`. This function takes an `IUser` object (typed in `packages/core-typings/src/IUser.ts`), typically obtained via the `useUser()` hook from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts` (`packages/ui-contexts/src/hooks/useUser.ts`), and maps its properties to the `AccountProfileFormValues` type. The `getUserEmailAddress` utility from `apps/meteor/lib/getUserEmailAddress.ts` is used within `getProfileInitialValues` to extract the primary email address from the user object. The actual form fields are rendered by the `AccountProfileForm` component (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/AccountProfileForm.tsx`), which accesses the form context using `useFormContext`. When a user saves changes, the `handleSave` function within `AccountProfileForm` dispatches updates to the server via the `/v1/users.updateOwnBasicInfo` endpoint and handles avatar updates using the `useUpdateAvatar` hook.

Rocket.Chat provides dynamic font size adjustments for accessibility. The core mechanism is encapsulated in the `useCreateFontStyleElement` hook, defined in `apps/meteor/client/views/account/accessibility/hooks/useCreateFontStyleElement.ts`. This hook returns a memoized function that, when called with a `fontSize` string (e.g., '100%', '120%'), creates or updates a `<style>` HTML element with `id="rcx-font-size"` in the document's `<head>`. The `innerHTML` of this style element is set to `html { font-size: ${fontSize}; }`, effectively applying the chosen font size globally. This hook is utilized in two main scenarios: first, by `useFontStylePreference` (`apps/meteor/client/views/root/hooks/loggedIn/useFontStylePreference.ts`), a root-level hook that reactively watches the user's `fontSize` preference (via `useUserPreference`) and applies it using `useLayoutEffect` during client startup or preference changes. Second, the `AccessibilityPage` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/accessibility/AccessibilityPage.tsx`) also uses `useCreateFontStyleElement` to immediately reflect font size changes made by the user on the accessibility settings page, specifically within the `onSettled` callback of the `setPreferencesAction` mutation.

The navigation items for the user's account settings are dynamically registered and managed through a centralized system. The `apps/meteor/client/views/account/sidebarItems.tsx` file is responsible for defining these items. It uses the `createSidebarItems` utility to generate a set of functions, including `registerAccountSidebarItem`, `unregisterSidebarItem`, `getAccountSidebarItems`, and `subscribeToAccountSidebarItems`. This file directly registers a predefined list of account sidebar items such as 'Profile', 'Preferences', 'Security', and 'Accessibility_and_Appearance'. Each item configuration includes its `href`, `i18nLabel`, `icon`, and crucially, a `permissionGranted` function. These `permissionGranted` functions dynamically determine item visibility by checking various `settings.watch` values (e.g., `Accounts_AllowUserProfileChange`, `Webdav_Integration_Enabled`) or user permissions using `hasPermission` or `hasAtLeastOnePermission` from `../../../app/authorization/client`.

The client-side Meteor layer provides reactive watchers to ensure that user data is always up-to-date across the application. The `apps/meteor/client/meteor/user.ts` file defines two key reactive functions: `watchUserId` and `watchUser`. The `watchUserId()` function uses a generic `watch` utility to observe changes in the `userIdStore` (from `apps/meteor/client/lib/user.ts`), providing the current user's ID reactively. Building on this, `watchUser()` first obtains the reactive user ID and then uses the `watch` utility to observe the `Users.use` store (presumably a client-side collection or state store for user data) to retrieve the full `IUser` object corresponding to that ID. This ensures that any component consuming `watchUser()` will automatically re-render when the user's data changes. The `useUser` hook from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts` (`packages/ui-contexts/src/hooks/useUser.ts`) is the primary interface for React components to access this reactive user data, reading directly from the `UserContext` which is populated by these underlying reactive data sources.

The client startup and account profile management in Rocket.Chat follow a clear data flow. User data, represented by the `IUser` type (`packages/core-typings/src/IUser.ts`), is reactively watched via `watchUserId` and `watchUser` (`apps/meteor/client/meteor/user.ts`), making it available through the `UserContext` and consumed by the `useUser` hook (`packages/ui-contexts/src/hooks/useUser.ts`). This reactive user object is crucial for initializing the `AccountProfilePage` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/AccountProfilePage.tsx`), where `getProfileInitialValues` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/getProfileInitialValues.ts`) populates the `react-hook-form` state. User interactions with the `AccountProfileForm` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/profile/AccountProfileForm.tsx`) trigger updates to the server via endpoints like `/v1/users.updateOwnBasicInfo`. Concurrently, client-side preferences, such as `fontSize`, are read from `user_preferences` by `useFontStylePreference` (`apps/meteor/client/views/root/hooks/loggedIn/useFontStylePreference.ts`) and applied to the DOM using `useCreateFontStyleElement` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/accessibility/hooks/useCreateFontStyleElement.ts`). The `Account Sidebar Items Configuration` (`apps/meteor/client/views/account/sidebarItems.tsx`) dynamically registers navigation links based on user permissions and system settings, ensuring a personalized and secure user experience.

Room Coordinator, Publications & Callbac.text: Rocket.Chat's architecture for managing rooms, data flow, and extensible logic relies heavily on three core components: the Room Coordinator, Meteor Publications, and the Server-Side Callback Pipeline. The Room Coordinator, with its client-side and server-side implementations, centralizes the configuration and behavior of different room types (e.g., public channels, direct messages). Meteor Publications handle the efficient, reactive data exchange between the server and connected clients, ensuring users see up-to-date room and message information. Finally, the Server-Side Callback Pipeline provides a powerful mechanism for injecting custom logic at various points in the application's lifecycle, allowing for flexible extensions and integrations without modifying core code. Together, these systems ensure a robust and adaptable framework for room management and real-time communication.

The `RoomCoordinator` is an abstract class defined in `apps/meteor/lib/rooms/coordinator.ts` that serves as the foundation for managing various room types within Rocket.Chat. It provides a standardized way to register room configurations (`IRoomTypeConfig`) and their associated behaviors (directives).Key functionalities of the base `RoomCoordinator` include:`addRoomType(roomConfig, directives)`: Registers a new room type, storing its configuration and client/server directives.`getRoomTypeConfig(identifier)`: Retrieves the configuration for a given room type.`getRouteLink(roomType, subData)`: Generates a client-side URL path for a room based on its type and data, utilizing the `route` defined in the `IRoomTypeConfig`.Two concrete implementations extend this base class:1.  **`RoomCoordinatorServer`** (`apps/meteor/server/lib/rooms/roomCoordinator.ts`):    *   Manages server-side specific directives (`IRoomTypeServerDirectives`) for room types.    *   The `add` method allows registering room types with default server-side behaviors, such as `allowRoomSettingChange`, `allowMemberAction`, `roomName`, `canBeDeleted`, and `getNotificationDetails`.    *   It provides methods like `getRoomDirectives(roomType)` to access these behaviors, `getRoomName(roomType, roomData, userId)` to retrieve a room's display name, and `setRoomFind(roomType, roomFind)` to register custom room finding logic for publications.    *   Examples of room types registered on the server include 'c' (public channels) via `getPublicRoomType` in `apps/meteor/lib/rooms/roomTypes/public.ts` and 'unread' via `getUnreadRoomType` in `apps/meteor/lib/rooms/roomTypes/unread.ts`.2.  **`RoomCoordinatorClient`** (`apps/meteor/client/lib/rooms/roomCoordinator.tsx`):    *   Handles client-side specific directives (`IRoomTypeClientDirectives`) and UI-related logic.    *   Its `add` method registers room types with client-side behaviors like `allowRoomSettingChange`, `allowMemberAction`, `roomName`, `getUiText`, `getAvatarPath`, and `canSendMessage`.    *   The `openRouteLink(roomType, subData, queryParams, options)` method is crucial for client-side navigation, using the `router.navigate` function to open specific room routes.    *   It also includes logic for determining if a room is read-only (`readOnly(room, user)`), considering room settings, user mutes, and permissions (`hasPermission` from `app/authorization/client`).    *   Client-side room types also define their routes, such as the `channel` route for public channels (`/channel/:name/:tab?/:context?`) as seen in `apps/meteor/lib/rooms/roomTypes/public.ts`.This coordinated approach ensures that both client and server can correctly interpret and act upon room-specific configurations and behaviors, providing a consistent experience across the application.

Meteor Publications are a fundamental part of Rocket.Chat's real-time data synchronization, allowing the server to push data to connected clients reactively. They are implemented as DDP methods and publications on the server.Key publications related to rooms and messages include:1.  **`rooms/get`** (`apps/meteor/server/publications/room/index.ts`):    *   This method, exposed via `Meteor.methods`, allows clients to fetch a list of rooms.    *   It supports fetching all rooms for a given `userId` or only public channels (`type: 'c'`) if `Accounts_AllowAnonymousRead` is enabled for anonymous users.    *   It also supports incremental updates by accepting an `updatedAt` timestamp, returning `update` and `remove` arrays for efficient synchronization.    *   The `Rooms.findBySubscriptionUserId` and `Rooms.findByDefaultAndTypes` methods are used to query the database.2.  **`getRoomByTypeAndName`** (`apps/meteor/server/publications/room/index.ts`):    *   This method allows clients to retrieve a single room by its `type` and `name`.    *   It performs crucial authorization checks using `canAccessRoomAsync` and `hasPermissionAsync` to ensure the requesting user has access to the room.    *   Notably, it integrates with the `RoomCoordinatorServer` by calling `roomCoordinator.getRoomFind(type)`. This allows room types to define custom logic for finding rooms, rather than relying solely on `Rooms.findByTypeAndNameOrId`. For example, a custom room type might need to perform a more complex lookup.    *   It also handles the `Store_Last_Message` setting, potentially removing `lastMessage` from the room object if the user lacks `preview-c-room` permission.3.  **`messages/get`** (`apps/meteor/server/publications/messages.ts`):    *   This method is responsible for fetching messages within a specific room (`rid`).    *   It supports various options for pagination, including `lastUpdate` for simple updates, and `latestDate`, `oldestDate`, `next`, `previous` for cursor-based pagination.    *   The `mountCursorQuery`, `mountNextCursor`, and `mountPreviousCursor` functions handle the complex logic of generating MongoDB queries and cursor strings for efficient message retrieval.    *   It uses `Messages.findForUpdates` and `Messages.trashFindDeletedAfter` to retrieve updated and deleted messages.    *   Access control is enforced via `canAccessRoomIdAsync`.4.  **`spotlight`** (`apps/meteor/server/publications/spotlight.ts`):    *   This method provides a search functionality for users and rooms.    *   It delegates the actual search logic to the `Spotlight` class.    *   It can search for users (`spotlight.searchUsers`) and rooms (`spotlight.searchRooms`) based on the provided `text` and `type` filters.    *   Rate limiting is applied to this method using `DDPRateLimiter.addRule` to prevent abuse.These publications collectively manage the flow of room and message data, ensuring that clients receive the necessary information while adhering to security and performance considerations.

The Server-Side Callback Pipeline, implemented by the `Callbacks` class (`apps/meteor/server/lib/callbacks/callbacksBase.ts` and `packages/ui-client/src/lib/callbacks/Callbacks.ts`), provides a powerful and extensible mechanism for injecting custom logic at predefined points (hooks) within the Rocket.Chat application's execution flow. This system allows developers to extend or modify core behaviors without directly altering the main codebase.Key aspects of the `Callbacks` system:    *   **Hooks**: Callbacks are registered against specific `hook` names (strings), which represent points in the application lifecycle where custom logic can be executed.    *   **`add(hook, callback, priority, id)`**: This method registers a `callback` function to a given `hook`.        *   `priority`: Callbacks can be assigned a `CallbackPriority` (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) to control their execution order. Callbacks with higher priority run first.        *   `id`: A unique identifier for the callback, preventing duplicate registrations.    *   **Types of Callbacks**:        *   `TChainedCallbackSignatures`: These callbacks are executed sequentially, where the output of one callback becomes the input for the next. This allows for transformation of data as it passes through the pipeline. The `createSequentialRunner` method handles this by `pipe`-ing callbacks.        *   `TEventLikeCallbackSignatures`: These callbacks are executed more like event listeners, typically for side effects, and do not necessarily modify the item being passed. The `createAsyncRunner` method handles these, often using `setTimeout` for non-blocking execution on the server.    *   **Execution**:        *   `run(hook, item, constant)`: Executes chained callbacks sequentially, passing the `item` through each callback.        *   `runAsync(hook, item, constant)`: Executes event-like callbacks asynchronously (server-side only).    *   **Server-Side Hooks**: The `apps/meteor/server/lib/callbacks.ts` file defines a comprehensive list of server-side hooks, demonstrating the wide range of extension points available. Examples include:        *   `afterSaveMessage`: Executed after a message is saved, allowing for post-processing or notifications.        *   `afterCreateRoom`: Triggered after a new room is created.        *   `livechat.closeRoom`: Invoked when a Livechat room is closed.        *   `beforeDeleteUser`: Allows logic to run before a user is deleted.By leveraging the Callback Pipeline, Rocket.Chat maintains a modular and extensible architecture, enabling features like integrations, custom business logic, and third-party app functionality to seamlessly integrate with the core platform.

The interaction between the Room Coordinator, Meteor Publications, and the Server-Side Callback Pipeline orchestrates a robust data flow within Rocket.Chat, particularly concerning room and message management.1.  **Client-Side Interaction and Routing**:    *   When a user interacts with the UI (e.g., clicks on a room in the sidebar), the `RoomCoordinatorClient` (`apps/meteor/client/lib/rooms/roomCoordinator.tsx`) is often the first point of contact.    *   It uses its `getRoomDirectives` and `getRoomTypeConfig` to determine room-specific UI behaviors (e.g., `roomName`, `readOnly`).    *   For navigation, `RoomCoordinatorClient.openRouteLink` utilizes the client-side `router` to navigate to the correct room path (e.g., `/channel/:name`) based on the room type's defined `route` in its `IRoomTypeClientConfig` (e.g., `apps/meteor/lib/rooms/roomTypes/public.ts`).2.  **Data Fetching via Meteor Publications**:    *   As the client navigates or requires data, it subscribes to Meteor publications or calls DDP methods.    *   For room lists, `Meteor.call('rooms/get')` (`apps/meteor/server/publications/room/index.ts`) fetches rooms, potentially using `updatedAt` for efficient synchronization.    *   To fetch a specific room, `Meteor.call('getRoomByTypeAndName', type, name)` is used. This method on the server consults `roomCoordinator.getRoomFind(type)` (`apps/meteor/server/lib/rooms/roomCoordinator.ts`) to apply room-type specific lookup logic before querying the `Rooms` collection in the `database`.    *   For messages, `Meteor.call('messages/get', rid, options)` (`apps/meteor/server/publications/messages.ts`) retrieves messages from the `Messages` collection, handling complex cursor-based pagination.    *   Search functionality is handled by `Meteor.call('spotlight', text, ...)` (`apps/meteor/server/publications/spotlight.ts`), which uses the `Spotlight` service to query `Users` and `Rooms` collections.3.  **Server-Side Logic and Extensibility**:    *   Server-side operations, such as saving a message or creating a room, often trigger the `Callbacks` system (`apps/meteor/server/lib/callbacks.ts`).    *   For instance, after a message is saved, the `afterSaveMessage` hook might be triggered, allowing registered callbacks to perform actions like sending notifications or updating external systems. These callbacks can be chained (`createSequentialRunner`) to transform data or run asynchronously (`createAsyncRunner`) for event-like processing.    *   The `RoomCoordinatorServer` provides room-type specific business logic on the server, such as `allowMemberAction` or `canBeDeleted`, which are invoked during various server operations.In essence, the `RoomCoordinator` acts as a central registry for room behaviors, guiding both client-side UI/routing and server-side business logic. `Meteor Publications` are the conduits for real-time data, ensuring clients have the necessary information. The `Callbacks` system provides the crucial extensibility layer, allowing the application to be customized and integrated without tight coupling, creating a flexible and powerful data flow.

Testing Infrastructure, Mocks & Fixtures.text: Rocket.Chat's testing infrastructure primarily leverages Jest, configured through a monorepo approach using shared presets from `@rocket.chat/jest-presets/client` and `@rocket.chat/jest-presets/server`. This setup allows for distinct testing environments for client-side (e.g., UI components, providers) and server-side (e.g., API endpoints, business logic) code. Mocks and fixtures are integral, with specific `moduleNameMapper` configurations in `jest.config.ts` files, such as mapping `meteor/(.*)` to dedicated mock files like `apps/meteor/tests/mocks/client/meteor.ts`, to isolate units under test.

The core Jest configuration resides in `apps/meteor/jest.config.ts`, which defines two main projects: `client` and `server`. The `client` project utilizes `client.preset` from `@rocket.chat/jest-presets/client` and includes `setupFilesAfterEnv` for client-specific test environment setup. It targets test files within `<rootDir>/client/`, `<rootDir>/ee/client/`, `<rootDir>/app/ui-message/client/`, `<rootDir>/app/ui/client/`, and `<rootDir>/tests/unit/client/` directories. Crucially, its `moduleNameMapper` aliases common React ecosystem packages to `node_modules` and maps `meteor/(.*)` to `apps/meteor/tests/mocks/client/meteor.ts` for client-side Meteor API mocking. The `server` project uses `server.preset` from `@rocket.chat/jest-presets/server` and focuses on server-side logic in `app/livechat/server/`, `ee/app/authorization/server/`, `ee/app/license/server/`, `app/cloud/server/`, `app/utils/lib/`, `server/lib/`, `server/services/import/`, `server/settings/lib/`, `server/cron/`, `app/api/server/`, and `app/version-check/server/`. Individual packages like `packages/mock-providers/jest.config.ts`, `packages/ddp-client/jest.config.ts`, `packages/ui-voip/jest.config.ts`, `packages/ui-kit/jest.config.ts`, `packages/fuselage-ui-kit/jest.config.ts`, `packages/ui-client/jest.config.ts`, `packages/gazzodown/jest.config.ts`, `ee/packages/license/jest.config.ts`, `ee/packages/omnichannel-services/jest.config.ts`, `ee/packages/federation-matrix/jest.config.ts`, and `ee/packages/presence/jest.config.ts` also maintain their own `jest.config.ts` files, predominantly extending either the client or server preset and sometimes adding package-specific `moduleNameMapper` entries for React dependencies or `modulePathIgnorePatterns` for test helpers.

While not explicitly tied to Storybook in the provided `jest.config.ts` files, the `packages/mock-providers` package is dedicated to providing mock implementations, as indicated by its `jest.config.ts` file. This package's tests are located in `<rootDir>/src/tests/**/**.spec.[jt]s?(x)`, and it uses `client.preset` from `@rocket.chat/jest-presets/client`. It also specifies `modulePathIgnorePatterns: ['<rootDir>/__tests__/helpers']`, suggesting that shared test helpers within this package are kept separate from the main test suite. These mock providers are likely consumed by other packages for unit and integration testing of components that rely on external services or complex states.

The primary mechanism for mocking external dependencies, particularly for client-side Meteor APIs, is through `moduleNameMapper` in `apps/meteor/jest.config.ts`. This configuration maps any import starting with `meteor/` to `apps/meteor/tests/mocks/client/meteor.ts`. This dedicated mock file is responsible for providing stubbed or controlled implementations of Meteor's client-side functionalities, which would include methods related to logging, data subscriptions, and method calls, effectively acting as an adapter mock for the Meteor framework. This allows client-side code to be tested in isolation without a live Meteor environment.

Shared test data and utility helpers are managed across different packages. Several `jest.config.ts` files, such as `packages/mock-providers/jest.config.ts` and `packages/ddp-client/jest.config.ts`, include `modulePathIgnorePatterns: ['<rootDir>/__tests__/helpers']`. This pattern indicates the presence of `__tests__/helpers` directories within these packages, which likely contain reusable functions, factories, or data structures to facilitate consistent test setup and data generation. Additionally, `ee/packages/license/jest.config.ts` specifically ignores `MockedLicenseBuilder` within its `__tests__` directory, pointing to a specialized helper for constructing license-related test data.

While the term "Page Objects" is not explicitly used in the provided `jest.config.ts` files, the extensive `testMatch` patterns for client-side tests in `apps/meteor/jest.config.ts` cover a wide range of UI components and views. These include `<rootDir>/client/**/**.spec.[jt]s?(x)`, `<rootDir>/app/ui-message/client/**/**.spec.[jt]s?(x)`, `<rootDir>/tests/unit/client/views/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}`, and `<rootDir>/app/ui/client/**/**.spec.[jt]s?(x)`. This structure implies that UI components are tested, and while not explicitly "Page Objects," the tests likely interact with the UI in a structured manner. Fixtures, in the sense of prepared test data, are implicitly handled by the "Shared Test Data Helpers" discussed previously, providing consistent data for these UI tests.

The presence of end-to-end (E2E) testing is explicitly acknowledged in `ee/packages/federation-matrix/jest.config.ts` through `testPathIgnorePatterns: ['<rootDir>/tests/end-to-end/']`. This indicates that a dedicated suite of E2E tests exists, likely involving API integration. While the specific data structures for these E2E tests are not detailed in the provided configuration, their exclusion from unit test runs suggests they operate with a different set of data and environment requirements, often involving a more complete system setup and realistic API interactions. Server-side API tests, such as those defined in `apps/meteor/jest.config.ts` for `<rootDir>/app/api/server/**.spec.ts`, also contribute to API integration validation, using data appropriate for their scope.

Jest Presets, Storybook & Developer Expe.text: The Rocket.Chat codebase leverages a set of dedicated packages to streamline developer experience for component development and testing. This includes `packages/storybook-config` for a consistent Storybook environment, `packages/mock-providers` to supply essential mocked contexts for isolated testing, and `packages/jest-presets` to standardize Jest configurations across different project types (client and server).

The core Storybook configuration is defined in `packages/storybook-config/src/main.ts` via the `baseConfig` function. This configuration specifies the location of stories (`../src/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx)`), integrates essential addons like `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `@storybook/addon-essentials`, `storybook-dark-mode`, `@storybook/addon-webpack5-compiler-swc`, and `@storybook/addon-styling-webpack`. It also sets `@storybook/react-webpack5` as the framework and configures TypeScript for `react-docgen`.

UI parameters and decorators are managed in `packages/storybook-config/src/preview.tsx`. This file sets global `parameters` for backgrounds, story sorting, layout, and custom `docs` container. Crucially, it defines `darkMode` themes for both dark and light modes, customizing properties like `appBg`, `appContentBg`, `barBg`, `brandTitle`, and `brandImage` using tokens from `@rocket.chat/fuselage-tokens/dist/surface.json` and project metadata. The `decorators` array includes a function that uses `useDarkMode` from `storybook-dark-mode` to dynamically apply the correct `PaletteStyleTag` from `@rocket.chat/fuselage`, ensuring theme consistency. It also imports global CSS from `@rocket.chat/fuselage/dist/fuselage.css` and `@rocket.chat/icons/dist/rocketchat.css`.

For enhanced documentation, `packages/storybook-config/src/DocsContainer.tsx` provides a custom `DocsContainer`. This component extends `BaseContainer` from `@storybook/blocks` and uses `storybook-dark-mode`'s `DARK_MODE_EVENT_NAME` to listen for theme changes, applying the appropriate `themes.dark` or `themes.light` from `@storybook/theming` to the documentation interface.

The `packages/mock-providers` package is central to providing isolated and controlled environments for testing components. Its `src/index.ts` exports a `mockAppRoot` function, which instantiates a `MockedAppRootBuilder`, and re-exports various specific mock context components.

The `MockedAppRootBuilder` in `packages/mock-providers/src/MockedAppRootBuilder.tsx` is a comprehensive class that sets up mocked versions of critical application contexts from `@rocket.chat/ui-contexts`, including `ServerContext`, `RouterContext`, `SettingsContext`, `UserContext`, `DeviceContext`, `TranslationContext`, and others. It also integrates `QueryClientProvider` from `@tanstack/react-query` and `I18nextProvider` from `react-i18next` to provide a fully functional, yet mocked, application root for component rendering.

Individual mock context components offer granular control:
*   `MockedDeviceContext` in `packages/mock-providers/src/MockedDeviceContext.tsx` provides a `DeviceContext.Provider` with predefined mock values, such as a 'granted' `permissionStatus`.
*   `RouterContextMock` in `apps/meteor/tests/mocks/client/RouterContextMock.tsx` supplies a `RouterContext.Provider` with mocked navigation and route-building capabilities, utilizing `path-to-regexp` for path compilation.
*   `TranslationContextMock` in `apps/meteor/client/stories/contexts/TranslationContextMock.tsx` sets up a `TranslationContext.Provider` with a mocked `translate` function, initialized with `i18next` and loading `en.i18n.json`.
*   `ServerProviderMock` in `apps/meteor/tests/mocks/client/ServerProviderMock.tsx` offers a `ServerContext.Provider` with mocked server interaction methods like `callEndpoint`. The `makeCallEndpoint` utility allows dynamic registration of endpoint mocks.
*   `QueryClientProviderMock` in `apps/meteor/client/stories/contexts/QueryClientProviderMock.tsx` wraps components with a `QueryClientProvider` from `@tanstack/react-query`, configuring default query options (e.g., `retry: false`, `gcTime: Infinity`) and custom `onError`/`onSuccess` handlers for toast messages.

The `packages/jest-presets` package provides standardized Jest configurations for different testing environments.

For server-side tests, `packages/jest-presets/src/server/jest-preset.ts` defines a Jest `Config` with `testEnvironment: 'node'`. It configures a `transform` rule to use `@swc/jest` for `m?(t|j)sx?$` files, enabling `sourceMaps` and setting `jsc.target` to `es2020` with TypeScript parsing. It also specifies `transformIgnorePatterns` to selectively exclude `node_modules` from transformation, ensuring efficient testing, and enables `collectCoverage`.

Client-side test setup is handled by `packages/jest-presets/src/client/jest-setup.ts`. This file performs global setup tasks, including extending `expect` with `toHaveNoViolations` from `jest-axe` for accessibility testing. It mocks various browser APIs and global objects crucial for client-side code execution in a Node.js environment, such as `globalThis.crypto` (using `node:crypto.webcrypto`), `globalThis.URL.createObjectURL` and `revokeObjectURL` (using `uuid`), `globalThis.ResizeObserver`, `global.navigator.serviceWorker`, and `globalThis.IntersectionObserver`. It also sets `globalThis.TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder` from `node:util` and imports `@testing-library/jest-dom` for extended DOM matchers.

Together, `packages/storybook-config`, `packages/mock-providers`, and `packages/jest-presets` form a robust ecosystem that significantly enhances the developer experience within the Rocket.Chat codebase. They provide consistent, isolated environments for developing and testing UI components, ensuring high quality, maintainability, and efficient development workflows across the project.

## Rocket.Chat — Developer Wiki Overview

Rocket.Chat is a self-hosted, open-source team-communication platform offering real-time messaging, omnichannel customer engagement, voice/video calls, federation, and a rich extension ecosystem — all designed so organizations retain full control of their data.

### High-Level Architecture

The platform is a **Meteor monolith at its core**, progressively decomposed into discrete microservices. The server side exposes a REST API and a DDP/WebSocket layer; the browser client is a React application assembled from a large library of packages. Key architectural layers are:

- **Data & Settings** — MongoDB-backed data models, typed with shared TypeScript contracts, driven by a runtime settings engine.
- **Server Services** — Startup orchestration, job scheduling, message pipeline, search, email, push, presence, and file storage, all wired through a microservice-capable bus.
- **Security** — Layered auth (local, LDAP, OAuth/SAML, 2FA, E2E encryption, ABAC roles).
- **Real-Time Transport** — DDP publications, streaming, VoIP (SIP/WebRTC), and video conferencing integrations.
- **Apps Engine** — A sandboxed Deno runtime that lets third-party apps extend the platform without touching core.
- **UI Layer** — React + Fuselage design system, UI Kit blocks, context/provider tree, and a growing set of shared component packages.
- **Integrations** — Webhooks, slash commands, Slack bridge, Matrix federation, WebDAV, and calendar connectors.

### Where to Start

New engineers should read **Server Core Services & Startup** first to understand the boot sequence, then **Core Data Models & Type Definitions** for the data layer, followed by **HTTP Router, REST API & Type Contracts** and **DDP Protocol, Realtime Streaming & Publications** to understand how clients communicate with the server. After that, explore the feature area most relevant to your team.
